articles.title: Six swans a swimming after Corby town centre rescue
articles.summary: They take a car ride back to their lakeside home after being seen swanning along the town's roads.
articles.body:
A family of swans spotted sitting in a town centre resident's garden "as if they were waiting for their taxi" have been safely transported to a nearby lake.

The two adults and four cygnets were first seen swanning around near a bowling green on Occupation Road, Corby, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.

When charity volunteers arrived from Cambridgeshire the next day, they found the birds sunning themselves on Hazelwood Road.

After being safely rounded up into big blue Ikea bags, they took a back-seat trip to a lake about a mile away.

When they arrived, Graham Porter and his colleague, from The Waterfowl Sanctuary in Godmanchester, had to first work out where the family had come from.

He said the boating lake - about two miles (3.2km) away - was ruled out when reports suggested there was not normally a family of swans based there.

Instead, they opted for Pen Green lakes, about a mile (1.6km) away, which seemed their most likely home.

Porter said after getting themselves ready to bag the bevy, "we told the parents what we were doing and started wrapping them for the journey".

"The poor babies were sleeping as I drove," he said.

"We sussed out the lake first and found someone looking perturbed as to why the swans weren't there, and he was greatly relieved to hear we had them and so helped us carry the six from the car."

Porter said while at the lakes, he cleared various brambles and fishing lines from the area.

The pair then wished the family well before heading back home.

The Golden Flashes are 3-5 coming off a 35-20 win over Akron, and they realistically need this to stay alive for bowl eligibility. Sacramento State is just getting going as an FBS and MAC program, and it's trying. It's been a rough run, going 1-7, with all seven losses to FBS teams by double-digits. articles.title: Maybank Championship: England's Charley Hull two shots off lead after opening round of LPGA Tour event in Malaysia
articles.summary: Opening round of LPGA's Maybank Championship in Malaysia sees France's Pauline Roussin-Bouchard outright leader by a shot; England's Charley Hull two off lead after birdieing two of final three holes; Live coverage continues on Friday on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
France's Pauline Roussin-Bouchard birdied her final three holes at the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club for an 8-under 64 and a one-stroke outright lead.

Roussin-Bouchard, whose rookie season on the tour was 2022, is still looking for her first LPGA win and has three top-10 finishes.

American Sophia Schubert, who also joined the tour in 2022 and has no wins and three career top-10 finishes, was tied for second place after a 65 with Miyu Yamashita, who won last year's Malaysian tournament after a three-way play-off.

Another French player, Perrine Delacour, shot 66 and was tied for fourth with Hull, who birdied two of her final three holes

Haeran Ryu, a major winner this year at the Women's PGA Championship and at the Evian Championship, withdrew before her first-round tee time for an undisclosed reason. She was the highest-ranked player in the tournament in the absence of No 1 Nelly Korda and No 2 Jeeno Thitikul.

Last week, Yuri Yoshida won the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea, the fourth Japanese player this season to win on the LPGA Tour, joining Yamashita, Shiho Kuwaki and Yuna Nishimura. Yoshida had a 69 Thursday.

Among the hazards at the Kuala Lumpur layout was the sight, captured on the television coverage, of a 3-meter (10-foot) monitor lizard eating a smaller animal near one of the lakes on the course.

articles.title: Trump: Judge would be held ‘fully responsible’ for anyone hurt on ‘absolutely disgusting’ East Potomac golf course
articles.summary: President Trump on Wednesday evening slammed U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes’s decision this week to extend an order blocking tree removal at a golf course in Washington, D.C., that he wants to renovate into a championship-level course. In a Truth Social post, the president wrote that his administration would hold Reyes “fully responsible for anybody…
articles.body:
President Trump on Wednesday evening slammed U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes’s decision this week to extend an order blocking tree removal at a golf course in Washington, D.C., that he wants to renovate into a championship-level course.

In a Truth Social post , the president wrote that his administration would hold Reyes “fully responsible for anybody who is hurt, or killed, on this very dangerous, dilapidated, and unsightly Golf Course.”

The judge granted a preliminary injunction earlier this month and scolded the Trump administration’s lawyers for failing to provide adequate notice before cutting down over 400 hundred trees in East Potomac Park.

“I trusted you all not to do precisely what you have done,” she said during an emergency hearing on Oct. 12, noting the government had lost “all of its credibility” in the case.

Under the order, the administration cannot cut down, alter or harm additional trees on the property, with exceptions made for public safety. The injunction also stipulates that the administration must provide 10 days’ notice before it closes the course or makes “irreversible” changes to its design.

In addition, Reyes called for a new hearing over the issue, after Trump vowed to press ahead with the project despite the rulings.

The park is home to three golf courses, including an affordable 18-hole public facility that serves tens of thousands of players per week. It is also a popular destination for runners, bikers and picnics.

In his late Wednesday post, Trump shared images of torn protective netting, yellow grass and feces from around the course, calling these conditions “highly dangerous, dilapidated, and absolutely disgusting.”

“The driving range should provide Golfers with stunning views of the Washington Monument, not of a barren, debris-ridden wasteland,” the president continued. “The driving range should NOT be a threat to life and limb.”

He also called the conditions a “National Disgrace” and vowed to turn the park into a “WORLD CLASS PUBLIC Golf Course that is AFFORDABLE for locals.”

articles.title: Sergio García abandona el LIV Golf y vuelve al DP World Tour mirando la Ryder Cup
articles.standfirst: El de Borriol confirma su salida del golf y se centra en el circuito que le voy nacer, los Majors e intentar clasificarse para el duelo Europa-Estados Unidos
articles.summary: El de Borriol confirma su salida del golf y se centra en el circuito que le voy nacer, los Majors e intentar clasificarse para el duelo Europa-Estados Unidos
articles.body: Sergio García volverá la próxima temporada al DP World Tour, el circuito que alumbró su figura en 1999 cuando tenía 19 años y en el que consiguió su primera victoria, el Abierto de Irlanda. Se confirma así la ruptura con el LIV Golf, el circuito que le fichó en 2022 y en el que ha capitaneado a los Fireballs. El golfista de Borriol emitió un comunicado el jueves en el que significaba su compromiso con esta liga, "aunque también mantengo mis opciones abiertas para un regreso al PGA Tour", circuito en el que no podría jugar en caso de clasificarse hasta agosto de 2027 por la cláusula de protección impuesta por el circuito americano a los jugadores del LIV Golf. Al mismo tiempo expresó su arrepentimiento de nuevo por el episodio con el que se despidió del Masters de Augusta -estrelló su driver contra el tee del hoyo 2-, indicando que el torneo de la chaqueta verde le había dado "alguno de los mejores momentos de su vida. Quiero demostrar lo que he aprendido después de mi comportamiento del año pasado". Finalmente ha recordado que 2027 será año de Ryder Cup. "Ese es otro de los objetivos de la temporada como los Majors y los grandes torneos", dejando la apuerta abierta de que si no lo lograse como jugador le gustaría participar de alguna manera en la cita de Adare Manor. Sergio se une a una salida masiva de jugadores que no seguirán en una posible aventura del LIV Golf 2.0. y que lo han hecho público, entre ellos, Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, David Puig, Lucas Herbert, Louis Oosthuizen, Branden Grace, Adrian Meronk, Ian Poulter...

articles.title: Austin Smotherman sets sights on earning Masters invite after picking up back-to-back PGA Tour wins
articles.summary: Austin Smotherman's back-to-back PGA Tour wins vault him to No. 54 in the OWGR, and now a coveted Masters invite hinges on cracking the top 50.
articles.body: Austin Smotherman earned his first win on the PGA Tour in early October at the Bank of Utah Championship, checking the box of fulfilling a lifelong dream. He needed all of 22 days to get back into the winner's circle at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship. Earning two wins in consecutive starts is not only career-changing, but it also brings new goals to the forefront, and the 32-year-old is by no means keeping the top one on his list a secret. With his two wins this fall, Smotherman has earned a spot on the PGA Tour's Championship Series debuting in 2028, exemptions into the 2027 PGA Championship and 2027 U.S. Open, and a touch more than $1.1 million. He also moved to No. 54 in the Official World Golf Ranking (OWGR), and now, moving up at least four spots and inside the Top 50 by year's end has understandably become the focus. "No doubt, no doubt," Smotherman began when asked if getting inside the Top 50 was now the top priority. "Everything for next year is already pretty firm as far as where things are going to be, but I still have majors that need to be put on the schedule. That’s the one thing that’s really shifted." PGA TOUR IS FINALLY BRINGING MATCH PLAY TO ITS POSTSEASON BEGINNING IN 2028 IN NO-BRAINER DECISION Players inside the Top 50 in the final edition of the world rankings in 2026 earn a spot in next year's Masters. Smotherman's lone major championship start in his career is a missed cut at the 2026 PGA Championship. "That’s why we wanted to go play Bermuda," Smotherman explained. "I got asked that question a lot last week, and my caddie did as well. From Monday through Friday, people were asking, 'What are you doing here? Why do you want to go to Bermuda? Why do you want to do this?' "My wife and I talked about it, and she’s got things handled at home. We’re in a good routine, and I didn’t go to Japan, so I got that extra week off. That’s what we were playing for. I’m going to play Austin and the RSM Classic to try to move inside the top 50. "If we’re 51st, we’re 51st. It’s not necessarily the end of the cutoff, because there are still other ways to get in and a little bit of time left, but having that certainty before taking time off would be nice." CAM YOUNG WAS OUT THE DOOR TO LIV GOLF, WIND CUTS PGA TOUR EVENT SHORT, AND GEARING UP FOR MEXICO Nice would be an understatement. Knowing a letter from Augusta National is on the way to your mailbox for next April's event before the calendar flips to 2027 would not only come with a sense of relief, but be a dream come true, which is a feeling Smotherman has managed to achieve on quite a consistent basis this fall. Smotherman, a former standout at SMU, defeated Seamus Power in a three-hole playoff in what was among the more unique finishes seen on the PGA Tour in quite some time. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Due to extreme winds ahead of the final round, the event was officially cut to just 54 holes, but with Smotherman and Power tied atop the leaderboard, the pair dueled it out on the tricky Par 3 16th hole on Monday morning until Smotherman's third consecutive par was enough to get the job done. Smotherman will enjoy the dad life at home in Dallas over the next couple of weeks while gearing up for his next start at the Austin Championship beginning on Nov. 12.

articles.title: Sergio Garcia Announces LIV Golf Exit, Will Play on DP World Tour For 2027 Season
articles.summary: Another marquee name is leaving the revamped LIV Golf behind.
articles.body:
Another marquee name is leaving the revamped LIV Golf behind.

Sergio Garcia announced Thursday he will play full time on the DP World Tour in 2027:

Grading Thursday's blockbuster NFL trade

"This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I'm proud to call it home again," he said. "I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour."

Garcia's decision comes as little surprise.

After filing for bankruptcy, LIV Golf laid out plans to transition to a "next phase." Nobody knows for sure what that structure will look like, but it's guaranteed to be a scaled down version in terms of schedule and purses.

As a result, a lot of LIV's most recognizable names are playing elsewhere next season.

The LIV defectors don't have a straightforward path to the PGA Tour. The tour's Returning Member Program from earlier this year only applied to a select few golfers and was open for a brief window.

As a result, the DP World Tour will become a big beneficiary for those who harbor aspirations of returning to the PGA Tour at a later date. In the case of Garcia, he needs to play high-level golf somewhere in order to fulfill his goal of competing on the Ryder Cup team.

The 46-year-old is past his prime, and his game likely suffered from his participation in LIV. His 2017 Masters victory is the last time he had a top-10 finish in a major tournament, while the 2019 KLM Open was the last DP World Tour win.

Playing a more regular schedule may allow for Garcia to rediscover enough sharpness to impress European captain Luke Donald ahead of the 2027 Ryder Cup.

articles.title: LIV Golf: Sergio Garcia 'open minded' about PGA Tour return as he targets 2027 Ryder Cup after breakaway league exit
articles.summary: Sergio Garcia has announced his intention to play on the DP World Tour in 2027 following his LIV Golf departure; the 46-year-old Spaniard is looking to secure a spot on Luke Donald's European Ryder Cup team for next year's tournament at Adare Manor
articles.body:
The 46-year-old Spaniard revealed his future plans in a statement on his social media accounts on Thursday. His departure from LIV Golf was already known after four years playing on the breakaway circuit.

"Next season, I'll be playing on the DP World Tour," Garcia wrote. "This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I'm proud to call it home again.

"I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour. And probably the most exciting part for me is strengthening my personal relationships, both new and old."

Garcia, who said he was "putting a big focus on a strong mindset and my mental health," also expressed his ambition to secure a spot on Luke Donald's European Ryder Cup team for the 2027 tournament at Adare Manor.

The Spaniard is Team Europe's all-time leading Ryder Cup points scorer with 28.5 points across 10 appearances, with his last coming at Whistling Straits in 2021.

Garcia's statement made reference to an incident at this year's Masters, where he broke his driver on the second hole at Augusta National after an outburst on the tee box. He was later issued with a code-of-conduct warning - a first at the tournament.

"I can't wait to get back to The Masters," added Garcia, who won the Green Jacket in 2017. "I left Augusta (in 2026) disappointed with myself and my actions, and I'm ready to show what I've learned and where I am mentally.

"Augusta has given me some of the greatest moments of my life, and I'd love nothing more than to chase another green jacket at such a special place."

The Spaniard was one of the most high-profile players to join LIV Golf in 2022.

His last start on the PGA Tour, outside of the majors, came at the Wells Fargo Championship that year. During that tournament, Garcia struck an errant approach shot into a patch of long grass and was overheard venting, "I can't wait to leave this tour," while looking for his ball.

Garcia, who has 11 career PGA Tour wins, will be forced to wait until August 2027 before he can make his return, due to the US circuit's 12-month suspension on LIV Golfers.

The circuit is emerging from Chapter 11 bankruptcy with BC Partners Credit and its $300 million pledge, and without Saudi money. Garcia had already sought - and been granted - approval to leave LIV.

Jon Rahm, Louis Oosthuizen, Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton are among other high-profile players to announce their exits from LIV .

articles.title: Sergio Garcia targets Ryder Cup return as he confirms LIV exit to rejoin DP World Tour
articles.summary: Sergio Garcia becomes the latest big name to quit LIV Golf and targets a Ryder Cup return after saying he will rejoin the DP World Tour.
articles.body:
Sergio Garcia has become the latest big name to quit LIV Golf while targeting a return to Europe's Ryder Cup team.

The one-time major champion said he will play on the Europe-based DP World Tour in 2027.

"This tour has been a huge part of my career from the beginning and I'm proud to call it home again," he said in a statement on social media. , external

The 46-year-old Spaniard added: "I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour."

Garcia won a combined 27 titles on the American and European circuits between 1999 and 2020, including the 2017 Masters.

He joined LIV in June 2022 after it launched as a Saudi Arabia-backed project but the former world number two will not be part of the second phase of the breakaway circuit.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing in April - having invested more than $5bn (£3.8bn) - leading to LIV filing for bankruptcy protection in the United States last month.

The league has secured a possible $300m (£224m) in financing to try to move forward with 'LIV 2.0' but only a handful of players have so far committed to the proposed competition in 2027.

Garcia follows top players Jon Rahm, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Graeme McDowell in announcing his departure.

In his statement, Garcia added that "the most exciting part for me is strengthening personal relationships, both new and old".

Garcia was sanctioned by the DP World Tour for breaking its rules when he defected to LIV, making him ineligible for the 2023 Ryder Cup.

The event's record points scorer had to settle outstanding fines - reported to be more than £1m - in order to be eligible for the 2025 edition, although ultimately he was not selected.

After helping Europe to six wins from 10 Ryder Cup appearances, he now hopes to return to their camp at Ireland's Adare Manor next year as a player or vice-captain.

"Another goal is to make that Ryder Cup team, and to be an asset to the guys in whatever capacity that may be," he said.

However, according to the current tour rules, while Garcia is eligible to play again, he cannot serve as a future captain or vice-captain.

Garcia may also face an awkward reunion with the PGA Tour.

Just before leaving for LIV in 2022, he told a rules official at the Wells Fargo Championship: "I can't wait to leave this tour. A couple more weeks and I won't have to deal with you any more."

He has remained eligible to play in majors and after hitting a poor shot at this year's Masters, Garcia ⁠slammed his driver into the Augusta turf and hit a nearby cooler, snapping the ​head ⁠off his club.

He apologised at the time and has now added: "There are some great tournaments around the world to play before Augusta next April, and I can't wait to get back to the Masters.

"I left Augusta last year disappointed with myself and my actions, and I'm ready to show what I've learned and where I am mentally.

"Augusta has given me some of the greatest moments of my life, and I'd love nothing more than to chase another green jacket at such a special place."

articles.title: By year-end, Delhi Metro's Magenta Line extension will connect four major stretches
articles.summary: Delhi Metro Magenta Line’s 6km Keshopur–Pushpanjali section with 6 elevated stations begins trials next month, opening by end-2026; Peeragarhi links Green Line.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The six-km Keshopur-Pushpanjali section — part of the 29-km Janakpuri West and RK Ashram Marg corridor and comprising six elevated stations — on Magenta Line is nearing completion. Its trial run is set to begin next month after which it is expected to open to public by 2026-end.Peeragarhi, an interchange station, will link this section to the existing Green Line. Other stations on this stretch include Keshopur, Paschim Vihar, Mangolpuri, West Enclave and Pushpanjali.With its opening, the Magenta Line extension will connect four major stretches: Green Line at Peeragarhi, Red Line at Pitampura, Yellow Line at Haiderpur Badli Mor and Pink Line at Majlis Park. “The Keshopur-Pushpanjali section is a key step in Delhi Metro Rail Corporation‘s (DMRC) Phase-IV expansion to improve accessibility and provide a direct, seamless link from northwest Delhi to south Delhi, Noida and IGI Airport Terminal 1,” said an official.“Civil work on the entire stretch has been fully completed and finishing touches are being given,” the official said.The station buildings have been designed with passenger convenience in mind. All stations, except Peeragarhi, have three levels: ground floor, first floor for concourse and second for platforms. “Peeragarhi has a different design as it is an interchange station. Its ground floor is for concourse, first has both concourse and platform facilities, and second accommodates a 160-metre-long foot overbridge connecting it to the Green Line station,” said the official, adding that a crossover has been provided on this stretch for train operations.These six stations will have modern amenities like passenger information display, public address systems, automatic fare collection gates, lifts, escalators and platform screen doors. “The corridor will be equipped with communication-based train control signalling and an unattended train operation system for greater safety, reliability and efficiency,” said the official.Entry and exit points have been planned according to the requirements of each station. Mangolpuri will have three entry and exit points, the most on this stretch, while West Enclave will have two, including an emergency exit.The Janakpuri West-RK Ashram Marg corridor comprises 22 stations. Two of its sections have already been commissioned: Janakpuri West to Krishna Park Extension (1.8 km) on Jan 5 this year and Deepali Chowk to Majlis Park (9.9 km) on March 8. With the opening of the latest six-km section, Magenta Line will become 55 km long and have 39 stations.Once the entire Janakpuri West-RK Ashram section becomes operational and after the addition of Central Vista corridor (RK Ashram to Indraprastha) and Indraprastha to Inderlok corridor, the total length of Magenta Line will further increase to 88.4 km, making it the longest in DMRC network. articles.title: Senators Look To Bounce Back In Los Angeles As Johansson Gets Third Straight Start
articles.summary: Thomas Chabot returns from injury as the Senators play in Los Angeles Thursday night.
articles.body:
The Senators will look to get their five-game road trip back on track on Thursday night when they face the Los Angeles Kings.

They opened their trip with a 4-1 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday, a game where they generated a pile of scoring chances.

Travis Green is glad to have all of his best defensemen finally be injury-free (Senators YouTube).

The Sens outshot Vegas 11-4 in the opening period and had several excellent opportunities to take control of the game. But the Golden Knights eventually broke a 1-1 tie midway through the third period and pulled away for the victory, sealed by two empty net goals.

The Senators enter Thursday's game with an 8-5-0 record, good for second place in the Atlantic. The Kings have struggled at 3-6-2, and the Sens would prefer not to hand them their first home win of the year.

With Linus Ullmark still out with a lower body thing, Jonas Johansson will make his third consecutive start in goal for the Senators. Johansson was recalled from the Belleville Senators just seven days ago, and appears to have quickly displaced Sam Ersson on the depth chart.

Johansson made his Sens debut in Saturday's 7-4 victory over the New York Rangers before getting another start against Vegas on Tuesday. He'll now get another opportunity to strengthen his grip on the backup role as Ullmark continues to recover.

For the first time all season, it'll be all hands on deck on the Sens' blue line. Thomas Chabot will return to the lineup after missing time with an injury. Chabot skated alongside Jordan Spence at Thursday's morning skate, while Jake Sanderson was paired with Artem Zub. Tyler Kleven and Nikolas Matinpalo formed the third pairing.

Chabot's return means Carter Yakemchuk sits out.

"Anytime you can get back to full health, it's a good thing for our group,' head coach Travis Green told the Senators website. "Obviously, Chabby is a big part of our team. It's not an easy decision on who to play tonight. We've got seven guys that we like a lot. LA is a big, strong team. They're heavy in front of the net, so we kind of based our decision on that."

Up front, the Senators will be without Warren Foegele, who suffered a lower-body injury during Tuesday's loss in Vegas. Green says Foegele is expected to be sidelined for an extended period, which means Hayden Hodgson will draw into the lineup.

Hodgson, who spent the 2023-24 season in the Kings organization, skated on the fourth line alongside Stephen Halliday and Nick Cousins.

The Senators have been a solid bounce back team this season. Despite five losses through their first 13 games, they have yet to lose consecutive contests.

Zetterlund – Stützle – Giroux Burakovsky – Cozens – Batherson Greig – Pinto – Amadio Hodgson – Halliday – Cousins

Sanderson – Zub Chabot – Spence Kleven – Matinpalo

The Kings defeated the Senators 2-1 in their most recent meeting.

The Sens are 3-3-0 on the road this season, while the Kings are still searching for their first home win.

Thursday's game is the second stop on a five-game road trip for the Senators.

articles.title: Choctawhatchee locks up 4th straight district with rout of Washington
articles.summary: Felling rivals and winning district titles, that's what Choctawhatchee football is about. On Thursday the Big Green shored up District 1-4A in a rout.
articles.body:
Choctaw rides ground game to rout of Niceville

FORT WALTON BEACH — There was no grandiose celebration of a four-peat, nor was there even acknowledgement of it by Frank Beasley in the postgame huddle.

Instead, after Choctaw (6-2, 4-0) won its sixth straight game and locked up District 1-4A again with a 49-7 win over Booker T. Washington (6-2, 3-1), the Big Green put their head down because they know what's on the horizon.

Region 1-4A is a gauntlet with unbeaten Columbia ranked No. 1, undefeated St. Augustine No. 2, unbeaten Mosley at No. 3 and Ed White 7-2 narrowly ahead of the Big Green at No. 4. That'll likely change between now and the next weekend before the region brackets are revealed, but for now the Big Green can only control what they can control.

"We're not affected by who we have to play in the playoffs, and we'll get the job done," senior Carter Marracco said.

"We just have to play Choctaw football," added senior Zeke Burgess.

Choctaw football is felling rivals and winning districts these days, and in convincing fashion too. In its 4-0 district stretch, Beasley's crew has outscored foes 182-29 with four running clocks. The Big Green will try to bolster their resume as much as possible Nov. 4 against district foe Fort Walton Beach in "The Game," and then they'll see where the chips fall with Region 1 still running through the defending-champion Big Green.

"Our guys just come out here and practice and we get ready to play and we move about our business and focus on ourselves," Beasley said. "Our kids don't mind getting on a bus. They're used to it anything thrown at them."

On Thursday, Choctaw was prepared to shine in all three phases of the game.

Marracco opened the scoring on the first play with a 69-yard keeper out of the wildcat, followed by a 26-yard touchdown from the right arm of Baker Giles.

"We were talking about it all week." Marracco said of the opening play. "The O-line opened up a great hole, I faked it to Dante and one of the linebackers bit and I just ran through the hole."

Dante Whidbee followed with a 44-yard touchdown to make it 20-0, and then Burgess stepped in front of an out-route and took it 24 yards to the house for a 28-0 lead after Marracco's 2-point conversion.

"That was third-and-3, so I just played the sticks," Burgess said. "They threw an out-route on the sticks where I was supposed to be, and I took it to the pick-six."

A 23-yard touchdown connection between Giles and DJ Spence capped the first half scoring to start the running clock out of the halftime locker room.

In the second half, Amir Reese tacked on an interception in the end zone, Isaiah Collins rushed for an 11-yard touchdown and Jabron Ruffin had a pick-six to make it 49-0. Pair that with a blocked punt and a forced and recovered fumble after a pinned punt, and Choctaw made a 6-1 team look like a freshman squad. In fact, Washington only scored in the waning seconds after a full second half against Choctaw's No. 2s.

"Practices have been really intense," Beasley said. "Coaches have done a great job of getting our kids ready; we were down a lot of starters tonight on defense, I think four. And our guys stepped in and did some really great things against a potent offense. They've really scored at a high clip with some really good receivers, a good quarterback and a really big O-line. Credit to coach (Terrence) Brooks and the staff for getting the kids prepared."

articles.title: Panthers QB Bryce Young addresses knee injury after Week 8 loss to Packers
articles.summary: Panthers QB Bryce Young was asked about his knee injury following Thursday night's loss to the Packers.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young isn't playing at 100 percent. But that, based off the reactions from head coach Dave Canales and Young himself, doesn't seem to be too great of a concern—at least for now.

Young's knee issue, which he sustained back in the Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns , has kept his name on the injury report for the last handful of games. The effects of that problem seemed most obvious on Thursday night, throughout the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers.

With his offensive line failing to keep the pocket clean time and time again, Young—as he usually would—opted not to use his legs to extend plays. He was pressured on a career-high 22 dropbacks, and attempted zero scrambles.

Canales was asked if he thinks Young has been hampered by the injury.

"Maybe," he replied. "I would say that he certainly doesn't look like he's got that quick make-you-miss kind of deal. But he was able to create some space for himself.

"But the rush got after us, and that's the bottom line. We gotta take care of that first part of it so we have an element of time to be able to execute the play."

Well, he's not wrong. The rush got after Young for a total of six sacks, forcing the Panthers to become one-dimensional on offense.

Young was later asked if the knee has been bothering him.

"I'm fine," he stated. "Everyone's dealing with something at this point in the year. It's football. Nothing like that is an excuse."

That knee might see an even tougher test in Week 9, when the Panthers host the daunting defense of the Denver Broncos .

articles.title: 'Enjoying the game has to be the fundamental,' says Tvesa Malik after top-10 finish at India Open
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For Tvesa Malik, a strong performance at the Women’s Indian Open was as much about mastering her mind as it was about getting her golf right.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For Tvesa Malik, a strong performance at the Women’s Indian Open was as much about mastering her mind as it was about getting her golf right. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, carding a four-round total of one-under 287 (71, 73, 71, 72) to emerge as one of three Indians in the top 10. With Vani Kapoor finishing second and Pranavi Urs sharing fourth place, the home contingent enjoyed an encouraging week at the event.“I think everyone can see it. I’ve always been really proud of how, despite how small the Women’s Golf Association of India (WGAI) started out and how few girls have been playing, so many have gone on to play in Europe and overseas. It’s not an easy standard,” said Tvesa.The progress, she added, has been building for years, with Aditi Ashok establishing herself internationally before Pranavi Urs and other Indian golfers delivered strong performances, including at the Asian Games. The recent Women’s Indian Open, she felt, was another encouraging sign of that development.The emergence of young talent has also caught her attention. Ojaswini Saraswat, who made the cut at the Women’s Indian Open at just 13, offered a glimpse of the potential among the next generation. For Tvesa, however, the key to nurturing young golfers is ensuring that the desire to play comes from within.“A lot of the time, it’s actually their parents who come and ask questions about how they should proceed. For me, it has always been about enjoying the game. That has to be the fundamental. If that is there, the sky is the limit,” she said.She added, “Parents have an important role in helping young players pursue their ambitions, but the goals must ultimately belong to the children themselves.”While younger players today have access to better information and are developing their games at an early age, Tvesa believes they must also learn to manage expectations. The competition is becoming younger and more intense, making it important to balance ambition with patience.Reflecting on Ojaswini’s achievement, she said, “You have to realize that you’re still so young and there’s so much time. Continue learning, ride that experience, and, at the same time, don’t set expectations so high that they become unrealistic.”Tvesa’s own performance at DLF was a reminder of the importance of that balance. The demanding course, known for punishing inaccurate shots and misplaced approaches, requires players to remain composed even when things do not go according to plan.While her ball-striking had been encouraging, she felt her mental approach made the bigger difference during the week.“This year, I felt a bit more accepting of the course. When you play there and you’re from there, the expectations are always high. It’s such a fine line between pushing yourself and almost holding yourself back,” she said.Tvesa, who is familiar with the DLF layout, explained that a single mistake can have a significant impact because of the course’s demanding nature. Accuracy off the tee and precise approach shots are crucial, while missing a green in the wrong place can make even saving par difficult.Her ability to accept those setbacks and move on was particularly encouraging. She recalled how her caddie praised her composure after the final round.“My caddie said the biggest thing was not actually what I had played, but the fact that I didn’t get upset. That impressed him the most,” she said.For Tvesa, patience was the key. Rather than allowing a mistake to affect the rest of her round, she reminded herself that more opportunities would come.That mental adjustment is also central to the challenge she is working to overcome in her professional career. Although she feels her technique has improved significantly, the results have not always reflected the quality of her game.Tvesa, who is married to fellow professional golfer Ajeetesh Sandhu, said, “Your technique is good enough when you’ve practiced and played for this long. Then you have to find the small things that give you an edge. Awareness is a big thing, understanding where I’m making mistakes and why, rather than just spending all my time working on technique,”.Beyond individual performance, Tvesa believes Indian women’s golf needs stronger institutional support to sustain its progress. Drawing on her experience competing on the Ladies European Tour, she pointed to systems in countries such as Sweden, Germany, and Australia, where players receive assistance with accommodation, coaching, physiotherapy, and training facilities.“It’s an expensive game to play, and support is necessary for everybody. Having a team around a player also provides mental reassurance when travel, fatigue, and changing conditions affect performance,” she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Packers' Jacobs says TD celebration that drew criticism was modeled after a gospel song
articles.summary: (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says he was paying homage to a gospel song rather than making light of his recent arrest when he briefly ha...
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says he was paying homage to a gospel song rather than making light of his recent arrest when he briefly had his hands behind his back while celebrating a touchdown Thursday night.

This was Jacobs' second game of the season after coming off the commissioner's exempt list . He was placed on that list after charges were filed against him in August stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.

Jacobs pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal destruction of property.

Jacobs had just scored on a 1-yard run in the second quarter of the Packers' 27-19 victory over the Carolina Panthers when he put his hands behind his back for a moment while accepting congratulations from teammates. The video garnered plenty of attention on social media as some who watched on television believed Jacobs was simulating getting handcuffed.

Jacobs said he instead was modeling his celebration after a gospel song called "Break Every Chain."

"The guys did it with me," Jacobs said. "I didn't think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way. But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

Jacobs said he had spoken with Savion Williams and other receivers before making his season debut, and they came up with the idea that he would do a celebration thanking God after his first touchdown of the season. That celebration happened Sunday, as he went to his knees and raised his arms aloft after scoring in a 20-17 loss at Detroit.

They also had planned this "Break Every Chain" celebration after his second touchdown of the season. When Jacobs was asked about putting his hands behind his back as part of the celebration, he noted that the telecast only showed a brief portion of what he did.

"It was more to it than that," Jacobs said. "They stopped showing the celebration after that. Like I said, it is what it is."

Jacobs hadn't been able to play or practice while he was on the commissioner's exempt list. He was removed from that list last week, enabling him to play again even though the NFLs investigation of him remains ongoing.

articles.title: Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back
articles.summary: England's Marco Penge was two shots off leader Karl Vilips after round one of the Mexico Open, while US Open champion Wyndham Clark shot a 69 as the only top 10 player in the field; watch live coverage of round two from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Friday
articles.body:
Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey.

The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver.

"Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit."

Kensai Hirata of Japan was a stroke back, and Ben Griffin was at 64 with Marco Penge, Garrick Higgo and Jeffrey Kang.

Alvaro Ortiz of Mexico opened with a 65. He earned his PGA Tour card for next year through the Korn Ferry Tour.

"It was lovely," Ortiz said. "Bogey-free, played really solid. I felt like I was just flowing the whole day. Gave myself a lot of chances. I think I did very well from tee to green, which makes it very nice on this golf course."

Ortiz won the event in 2021 when it was part of the PGA Tour Latinoamerica schedule. The World Wide Technology Championship is next week at El Cardonal at Diamante in Los Cabos.

Vilips won the 2025 Puerto Rico Open for his lone PGA Tour title, making him exempt on the tour through next season.

The former Stanford player is 141st in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, with many players fighting to get into the final top 100 to remain on the tour.

Hirata is trying to move up from 170th. He made a 20-foot eagle putt on No. 3 and holed two birdie putts outside 20 feet.

"It was a perfect 7-wood distance and I hit a perfect 7-wood shot, which left me a really easy left-to-righter," Hirata said about the eagle. "Then that went in and kept the momentum going the rest of the back nine."

Penge is 112th in the standings. He had an 18-foot eagle putt on No. 3.

"I feel like I haven't actually played that much this year," Penge said "I've only played 18 tournaments due to, obviously, health issues. I'm just trying to get back fit really."

Defending champion Brian Campbell shot a 67.

Tom Kim also was at 67. He's playing for the first time since he won the gold medal in the Asian Games, which excuses him from mandatory military serve in South Korea.

U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark had a 69. He's the only player from the top 10 in the world in the field. John Daly II, the son of the two-time major champion, opened with a 70. He's playing on a sponsor exemption.

articles.title: Forest Green launch legal action over Savage approach
articles.summary: Forest Green chairman Dale Vince announces the club is taking legal action against Peterborough United.
articles.body:
Forest Green Rovers owner Dale Vince says the club has launched legal action against Peterborough United over its approach for former manager Robbie Savage.

The Welshman left earlier this month to join the League One side, despite Vince initially blocking the discussions. Vince later claimed he was forced to agree to the move when the 51-year-old was approached directly.

Vince made the announcement in a short video on social media , revealing Forest Green had "begun a legal process for the tapping up of our manager, now ex-manager, Robbie Savage".

Peterborough United offered no comment on the legal action when contacted by BBC Sport, but have previously denied making an illegal approach for Savage.

Savage joined Forest Green Rovers after a successful stint at the then-seventh tier Macclesfield FC - the phoenix club formed after Macclesfield Town was wound up in 2020.

During his time with the Silkmen, the club sealed promotion to National League North, scoring 109 goals and winning 109 points.

When he arrived in Gloucestershire in July 2025, he went on to guide Forest Green to the play-offs with the campaign ending in defeat to Boreham Wood.

It would turn out to be his only full season in charge, with Savage leaving the club on 2 October, with them sitting 13th after 11 matches .

At the time, Vince told BBC Radio Gloucestershire that he initially refused Peterborough permission to speak to Savage but relented after he said the club approached him directly.

"Peterborough themselves have covered themselves in no glory here. They came to us and said, 'We would like to speak to your manager,'" he told BBC Radio Gloucestershire 10 days after the appointment.

"We said no, and so they spoke to him, and then he came to us and said, 'I hear Peterborough want to speak to me.' So, that's an illegal approach."

Posh chairman Darren MacAnthony hit back against the claims, writing on X that the process to appoint a new manager was "100% correct and proper, following all the rules".

Since joining Peterborough, Savage's record has been two wins, two draws and two losses in all competitions.

articles.title: Mayor defects from Greens after 'Zionism is racism' motion
articles.summary: Drew Creek joins the Labour party after the policy motion was passed earlier this month.
articles.body:
The leader of the Green Party on Cornwall Council has defected following the party's recent "Zionism is racism" motion.

Drew Creek joined the Labour and Co-operatives on Thursday after the policy motion was passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.

Creek, who is Mayor of Newquay and serves as a councillor for Trenance ward, said he had "huge respect" for Greens across Cornwall but the motion "crossed a line".

The Cornwall Green Party said it was "deeply saddened" by Creek's decision to join Labour and said it does not "try to impose uniformity of belief" among its members and elected representatives.

The motion backed by Green members at its party conference said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It has been criticised by Jewish groups , as well as some Green MPs and opposition political parties .

Creek said he hoped the Green Party would step back from the stance – but said instead, "Zack Polanski and the leadership has doubled down".

"I can't stand behind that, and I won't pretend otherwise," the councillor said.

He added: "People in Newquay don't want politicians driving division. They want someone who'll fix the roads, protect our coast, fight for local services and bring people together.

"That's the kind of politics I believe in and the kind of politics Andy Burnham has shown.

"Newquay is my home and where I am raising my family. I came into politics for one reason, to stand up for this town and the people in it. Labour is where I believe I can do that best, and I'm looking forward to getting on with the job."

Councillor Kate Ewert, Labour and Co-operative Group Leader on Cornwall Council said Creek's decision "highlights the serious questions about Zack Polanski's leadership".

Noah Law, MP for St Austell and Newquay, added: "In this period of polarised politics, it takes great courage to stand up for what you believe in.

"Having worked with Drew since my election, I have always found him to be steadfast in his beliefs, easy to work with, and a good advocate for Newquay."

A spokesperson for the Cornwall Green Party said Creek had "done excellent work as a Green councillor" and they understood there were "different views within the Green Party on the 'Zionism is Racism' motion".

They said: "Disagreements over the wording of this one motion should not distract from the fact that the Green Party is united in its condemnation of the racist genocide and ethnic cleansing that Israel is perpetrating in Gaza and the occupied territories, and united in its demand for much tougher sanctions on Israel.

"Labour, by contrast, refuses even to recognise that what we are seeing is genocide, and continues to allow arms exports to and intelligence-sharing with the government that is committing it.

"It's hard to see how anyone who is serious about action on climate, action to end extreme inequality, and action to prevent an ongoing genocide could switch their support to a party that is not serious about any of these."

articles.title: Brooks Koepka Shades Bryson DeChambeau Over Rory McIlroy Feud in Video, 'Lives In His Own World'
articles.summary: Brooks Koepka made it clear this week who he is siding with in the dispute between Bryson DeChambeau and Rory McIlroy.
articles.body:
Brooks Koepka made it clear this week who he is siding with in the dispute between Bryson DeChambeau and Rory McIlroy.

Appearing Thursday on the Dan on Golf YouTube channel (beginning at the 23:15 mark) , Koepka was asked about DeChambeau taking issue with McIlroy not speaking to him during the final round of the 2025 Masters:

"[McIlroy] shouldn't have," Koepka said. "[DeChambeau] lives in his own world. I don't think many people want to talk to him regardless. I wouldn't have spoken to Rory and I don't think Rory would have spoken to me, and it would have been totally fine."

After McIlroy held on to win the 2025 Masters and complete the career Grand Slam, DeChambeau spoke about the communication between himself and McIlroy, or lack thereof, during the last round.

"Didn't talk to me once all day," DeChambeau told reporters . "He wouldn't talk to me. He was just like—just being focused, I guess. It's not me, though."

During the 2026 Open Championship in July, McIlroy criticized DeChambeau for suggesting he would perhaps pull out of the tournament after incurring a two-stroke penalty.

McIlroy told reporters , "I won't pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I'm not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it's performative. I think a lot of it's for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn't feel like it was a great look."

Koepka and DeChambeau have sometimes been at odds over the years as well, so it isn't surprising that Koepka is backing McIlroy.

During the 2021 PGA Championship, Koepka went viral for rolling his eyes at DeChambeau and criticizing him during an interview.

Koepka beat DeChambeau in a match play event at Wynn Golf Club in Las Vegas later that year, adding even more fuel to their rivalry.

Now, after a three-year run with LIV Golf, Koepka has been back with the PGA Tour since January, meaning he is no longer part of the same tour as DeChambeau.

articles.title: Brooks Koepka Exposes The PGA Tour’s Two-Tiered Rules
articles.summary: Brooks Koepka claims players get away with improving lies and trenching on greens. The five-time major winner argues the honor system has failed the game.
articles.body:
Brooks Koepka has thrown down the gauntlet regarding the integrity of professional golf. The five-time major champion suggests the PGA Tour struggles to police players who bend the rules to gain an edge. On his YouTube channel, Dan Rapaport heard Koepka speak frankly about the shady tactics he witnesses every day on tour. He pointed specifically to players fixing their lie in the rough and tapping down spike marks on the greens.

Koepka noted that guys get away with improving their lies more because you're are not right on top of them. He described a scenario where one player hits a shot while another is over in the left rough fixing the grass. The five-time major winner asked the tough question, according to Golf Monthly : "So I might be over there hitting my shot, but you're over here in the left rough and guys definitely do it, but it's just how are you going to prove it?"

Recent events prove Koepka's point about inconsistent enforcement. At Royal Birkdale during the 2026 Open Championship, Bryson DeChambeau was penalized two shots for improving his lie. Yet, Wyndham Clark faced no action from USGA officials after fans flagged his practice swings and club position at Shinnecock Hills during the US Open. This disparity creates a system where rules apply differently based on who is playing.

Koepka witnessed a specific incident this year that he deemed really bad. He saw a player chip the ball and realized the lie was fixed. The golfer went for a backswing and the whole ball was visible. Koepka admitted he could not prove the infraction. "What am I going to do? I can't prove it, and like at the same time, I understand guys have got to put the club down here, but if you keep putting the club down of course…" he said. The game relies on an honor system that clearly fails when the money is on the line.

The problem extends beyond the rough to the putting surfaces. Koepka criticized the trend of players using their putters to tamp down spike marks excessively. This practice, often called trenching, creates a channel for the ball to roll. He noted that the greens get very chewed up around the hole lately. He suspects this damage is linked to more players using AimPoint. "It's not good. It gets very chewed up around the hole lately and I don't know if it's because more people are doing AimPoint," Koepka stated.

He observed that players are close to the hole when they perform this action. Koepka is not a fan of the technique. "But yeah, not a huge fan of it, they do it in front of the ball and behind the ball," he said. The damage is visible to anyone watching closely, yet the tour seems unwilling to crack down hard enough to stop it.

Despite the rule-bending chaos, Koepka remains confident in his own game. He claims he knows if he will contend for a major before the week even starts. After his first practice round on Tuesday, he feels a specific level of confidence. "I feel like every time I've contended in a major, contended in a big moment, I kind of know it's going to happen before the week's already started. It's a weird feeling," he told Rapaport, according to Yahoo Sports .

His strategy for these big moments is simple: avoid disaster. Koepka's theory since day one is to not make a double bogey. He would rather take a safe shot and make a bogey than risk a double. This discipline helped him win the 2018 PGA Championship even after he made a double bogey on his way to the title.

articles.title: TGRERA bars sale of nine flats in Tellapur project after double-sale allegations
articles.summary: TGRERA restrains developer from selling or mortgaging nine Tripuras Green Alpha flats in Tellapur after double-sale allegations; interim order dated Oct 29.
articles.body: Hyderabad: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (TGRERA) has restrained a developer from selling, mortgaging or creating third-party rights over nine flats in a residential project at Tellapur in Sangareddy district, citing allegations of double sales involving other units in the same project.In a common interim order dated Oct 29, the authority observed that the developer’s counsel did not deny the earlier double sales but submitted that alternative units would be allotted. It held that the nine complainants’ apprehensions of similar transactions were genuine and warranted protection.The complaints concern flats in Tripuras Green Alpha at Tellapur village in Ramachandrapuram mandal. Buyers alleged that they had paid the entire or a substantial portion of the agreed sale consideration, with receipts acknowledged by the developer. Despite delays beyond the committed timeline, the developer allegedly demanded additional amounts instead of executing sale deeds. The complainants also alleged threats to cancel their allotments and sell the flats to third parties.The protected properties are flats 411, 1006, 608, 502, 811, 210 and 503 in Block A, and flats 404 and 906 in Block E.Following a hearing on Oct 9, TGRERA observed that allowing further sales could trigger fresh litigation and render its eventual orders ineffective. Finding a prima facie case of payment and allotment, it held that the balance of convenience favoured protecting the properties. articles.title: Panthers HC Dave Canales explains his decision to fire DC Ejiro Evero
articles.summary: Panthers HC Dave Canales took questions about the firing of DC Ejiro Evero.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales had, at least in the past, described his pairing with defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero as a dream. Well, it seemed to have turned into a nightmare on Mint Street.

Canales took the lectern this afternoon, and addressed today's firing of Evero . When asked what led to the move, he pointed to the outlook of the (hopefully) salvageable 2026 season.

"There's just collecting a lot of information over the course of our time that really led to the decision," Canales stated. "Ultimately—when I look at how many games we have in front of us, the position we're at in the division and really just wanted to get the most out of our guys.

"And really, making that decision, I take that responsibility very seriously as the head coach, and I know it's my responsibility to put the players in a position where they feel confident, where they feel ready to go.

"So, just took in a lot of information and came to this conclusion at this point, right now to be able to lay the groundwork for the style of football we wanna play."

That style couldn't have been what we've seen in the past two weeks, specifically last Sunday's embarrassing 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . The Bucs ran over the Panthers for nearly 260 combined rushing yards and three touchdowns, and threw the ball just 11 times.

On Thursday night, in the 27-19 defeat to the Green Bay Packers, Evero failed to scheme up pressure. Despite blitzing on nearly half of Green Bay's dropbacks, the Panthers recorded zero sacks and zero hits on quarterback Jordan Love.

Canales, who added that owner David Tepper and general manager Dan Morgan were consulted on the matter, was then asked what he'd like to see as a result of the change.

"Just wanna see the guys connected," he replied. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort's been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit."

"And for me, philosophically speaking it starts with the run game. It starts with owning first and second down, and being able to be aggressive and attack in different ways."

Defensive line coach Todd Wash, who has been with the organization since 2023, has taken over as the interim defensive coordinator.

articles.title: Judge to investigate whether Trump administration lied in golf course renovation case
articles.summary: A judge grilled Trump lawyers about what they knew of plans to close the golf course next month and said .
articles.body:
A US judge said on Friday that she will launch an investigation into whether justice department lawyers deceived her about President Donald Trump's plans for renovating a golf course.

Trump has posted on social media that the East Potomac Golf Course would be closed in November for several months for the renovations, despite an ongoing legal challenge.

The judge is looking into whether the administration's last-minute notification to her about removing trees from the course was made in bad faith, and if government lawyers misrepresented Trump's renovation plans.

Trump, an avid golfer, has said his plans will create "one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World".

He has called the 106-year-old course "Trash Island", saying it will be renovated over the course of 15 months to create a space that "will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments".

The legal dispute goes back to February, when the DC Preservation League and others sued over redevelopment plans for the park.

It escalated this month when the National Park Service began to cut down hundreds of trees without notifying the judge presiding over the lawsuit, US District Judge Ana Reyes, until 15 hours before work was set to begin on a holiday weekend.

After the trees were cut, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to stop tree removal until at least 26 October and give her three business days' notice about making any other permanent changes.

In a 70-page ruling this week, she extended that order and also barred the administration from making further alterations to the course without ten days' notice while the lawsuit proceeds. The administration has notified the court it intends to appeal that ruling, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

Despite the court-ordered block, Trump had recently announced that the course would be closed for 15 months beginning in November to accommodate the renovations. He also shared a rendering of the course redesign.

Government lawyers this week confirmed to Reyes that the course would be closed for renovations, after telling her earlier there were no plans to shutter it.

Reyes took a harsh tone with the lawyers at Friday's hearing, repeatedly questioning when they had knowledge of the plan to close the golf course.

At one point, she asked whether the Secretary of the Interior was involved in the project.

Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward - the number three official at the justice department - responded by asking what she meant by "involved".

Reyes then read the definition of the word from a dictionary.

At the end of the hearing, Reyes said she would be investigating whether the justice department attorneys "have made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules".

That included whether giving late notice to the court about the renovation plans was "done in bad faith" and whether the attorneys failed to correct previously false statements or withheld information.

She said she would carry out the inquiry with a special master, an independent third party. In the US, judges appoint special master to carry out investigations or other provide other legal work related to cases and disputes.

articles.title: US judge orders ethics inquiry into Trump lawyers over golf course case
articles.summary: Judge Ana Reyes calls on US government lawyers to explain contradictory statements about the East Potomac Golf Links.
articles.body:
A United States federal judge has opened a “formal inquiry” into whether US government lawyers misled the court over plans to transform a historic public golf course in Washington, DC.

Friday’s manoeuvre escalates an ongoing legal fight over President Donald Trump’s efforts to reshape the US capital.

Judge Ana Reyes of the US District Court for the District of Columbia announced she would appoint a special master to examine whether government officials withheld information or made misleading assertions concerning the East Potomac Golf Links.

The inquiry will not establish whether government lawyers committed misconduct. It will instead determine whether their conduct breached professional or ethical obligations.

The inquiry follows a series of contradictory statements by administration officials about plans to renovate the course, notably after Trump announced he would proceed with the project on social media.

Reyes questioned Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr for more than two hours during Friday’s hearing, repeatedly comparing his testimony with the president’s online announcements.

She also asked him whether a National Park Service official had been instructed to omit details from a court declaration.

Trump’s posts, which began earlier this month on his Truth Social account, indicated the course would close for 15 months, starting on November 15, to accommodate a major redevelopment.

Yet officials from various government agencies – including the Interior Department, Justice Department and National Park Service – had previously been unable to confirm the existence or scope of any plans when questioned by the judge.

Earlier this year, Reyes had ordered the government to provide advance notice of substantive construction work at the site.

But despite her order, the dispute intensified earlier this month after more than 400 trees were removed from the golf course. Reyes subsequently extended her injunction against the government making any further “irreversible” changes to the site.

On Wednesday, the Justice Department informed the court that the National Park Service would submit a design from golf course architect Tom Fazio to the National Capital Planning Commission on Friday.

But Justice Department lawyers had, up to that point, declined to acknowledge any plans with regards to the golf course.

Even before Wednesday’s submission to the court, Trump had posted about commissioning Fazio “to build a World Class Championship Golf Course” on the park site, which currently includes biking and walking paths.

The DC Preservation League, which filed the lawsuit in February, has argued the redevelopment could violate environmental protections and damage a historically significant public space.

The case marks one of two legal battles unfolding over Trump’s plans for Washington, DC, on Friday.

Another US judge is due to hear a separate challenge to the White House’s proposed construction of a 75-metre (250-foot) memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

The lawsuits raise broader questions about the limits of presidential authority over federal land and public monuments.

David Super, a professor at the Georgetown University Law Center, told The Associated Press news agency that the cases reflect a shift in how the administration approaches legal constraints on executive power.

“There was always the assumption that you would try to do things that were legal,” Super said. “What we’re seeing here now is that if you think the federal courts can’t stop you”, you can break the law.

articles.title: Mexico Open: Andrew Novak pulls three shots clear following late surge on Friday as Hawaiian sensation Kihei Akina shines
articles.summary: Andrew Novak finished strongly and leads a group of five players by three shots heading into the weekend; Hawaiian hotshot Kihei Akina continued his run of excellent form as he attempts to secure a PGA Tour card; watch live coverage of round two from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Saturday
articles.body:
Novak drove the reachable par-four 13th and holed a 12-foot eagle putt as he jostled with Ben Griffin to carry the lead heading into the weekend at Vidanta Vallarta.

But on 15, Griffin drove into the water and had to scramble for a bogey, while Novak holed a birdie putt from just outside 15 feet for a two-shot swing.

Novak closed with a 20-foot birdie putt to finish at 14-under through the opening two rounds, three shots clear of a group of five players that included Griffin (67) and Kihei Akina, the 20-year-old Hawaiian sensation who shot a 64 to post his ninth round of 67 or lower in his last four PGA Tour starts.

Also in the mix were France's Matthieu Pavon (66), Belgium's Adrien Dumont du Chassart (67) and Kensei Hirata of Japan (68).

"There's a pretty bunched leaderboard, said Novak. "I separated a little bit, but we're halfway there, there's so much golf to play.

"I'm going to have to go out and keep hitting a bunch of fairways. If I'm hitting my irons like this, I'm going to be able to give myself a lot of opportunities.

"I don't know if I'll make as many putts as I did today, but as long as I'm maximising my opportunities and make a few of those with the putter, I should be in a good spot."

Akina chipped in for birdie on the last hole Friday to continue an excellent run of form which has him eight points away from the 20 required for a US college golfer to secure a PGA Tour card.

"I'm feeling more comfortable with each round played," said Akina, who made three birdies on the par fives and picked up an eagle on the reachable par-four 13th when he drove the green from 296 yards.

"We had about 287 to the front of the green and that's what I was trying to hit," he said. "So just a nice, roasted draw mini-driver for me, landed in a perfect spot and rolled down to tap-in. So that was a bonus for me."

His life dream is to play on the PGA Tour and he's making remarkable progress, having already secured a top-10 finish in the Bank of Utah Championship. Dating back to August and the Wyndham Championship, Akina has picked up seven points in the PGA Tour University program for underclassmen and gets one point for every PGA Tour cut and one point for a top 10.

"I've just got to keep playing well and keeping my foot on the gas," he said. "Feel like I'm doing that pretty well this week."

articles.title: Maybank Championship: Miyu Yamashita in command as Charley Hull and Lottie Woad fall away in Kuala Lumpur
articles.summary: Leader Miyu Yamashita is aiming to defend a title for the first time in Malaysia; Yan Liu was the star of the field, shooting 63 on Saturday; Lottie Woad shot 65 but is 10 shots back; watch the final round from 1.30am on Sunday on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Mix
articles.body:
The 2025 Women's British Open winner and second-round leader had a 54-hole total of 198 to sit 18-under par overall at the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course.

"It was a very nice round today as well," said Yamashita. "I had a few tricky situations during the round, but I managed to get through them and finish without dropping a shot, so I'm really pleased with that.

China's Yan Liu had the round of the day on Saturday, a 63 which included an eagle, nine birdies and two bogeys, to move into a tie for second place. Pauline Roussin-Bouchard, who led after the first round and shot 67, was level with Yan, who is aiming to keep a steady mindset heading into the final round.

"I just really enjoyed today," said the Chinese player. "I think my swing is in very good position and my putting [was] on fire today. Yeah, really happy for my putter, and I hope tomorrow it's [the] same.

"One shot at a time, just live in the present."

Yamashita won last year's Malaysian tournament after a three-way playoff, and is looking to defend a title for the first time in Kuala Lumpur on Sunday.

"Of course winning a title is something pretty special itself, but I really like the course and I've been getting so much support from the fans here in Malaysia so I will do my best here tomorrow," she added.

Last week, Yuri Yoshida won the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea, becoming the fourth Japanese player this season to win on the LPGA Tour, joining Yamashita, Shiho Kuwaki and Yuna Nishimura. Yoshida shot 66 on Saturday to finish at 11-under par overall.

The two top English players will require a huge surge on Sunday to hope to compete. Charley Hull's 72 leaves her at nine under and tied for 18th, with Lottie Woad's impressive 65 on Saturday moving her above her compatriot to 10-under par - some eight shots adrift of the leader.

articles.title: Meet Peepal Baba, 80, and his green legacy around Sonepur village
articles.summary: 80-year-old “Peepal Baba” Bira Meher of Odisha’s Sonepur has spent 60 years planting and caring for peepal and banyan trees, creating a green legacy.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: At 4 am every day, when most people are still asleep, 80-year-old Bira Meher sets out from his home in Sahala village under Dunguripali block of Sonepur district to tend to the peepal and banyan trees he has planted over the past six decades.Known locally as ‘Peepal Baba’, Meher has planted trees wherever he has travelled, often carrying saplings and seeds. Over the years, he has nurtured them with the patience and dedication of someone raising a family.Meher says he hasn’t kept a count of the trees he planted over the years. “But all the peepal and banyan trees you see within a radius of nearly 10 km from my village have been planted by me at some point of time in my life. What matters is that many of the saplings have survived and grown,” he said.He developed an interest in growing trees after watching his father grow different varieties of plants on their ancestral farmland. But it was the large-scale felling of trees for road-widening projects that turned this childhood influence into a lifelong mission. His own village, too, lost many trees in the name of development, leaving him deeply disturbed.He chose peepal and banyan because they grow into large trees and require relatively little care. For him, however, planting a sapling is only half the job. Ensuring that it survives is a bigger job.That belief explains his daily routine. He has kept sticks and plastic containers at several spots so he can attend to the saplings whenever necessary.He draws water from nearby tubewells and canals, collects seeds and saplings throughout the year, and looks for suitable places to plant them, particularly during the monsoon.His commitment to the trees has remained undiminished even as he has grown older. His two sons are engaged in business, and he helps them with their work. But tending to the trees has become his principal pursuit. Meher also cleans the area near the trees he has planted.He, however, gets distressed at the sight of a tree being felled or when goats are allowed to roam freely and feed on the young plants he has painstakingly raised.“I hope people realise that planting a tree, particularly easily found native species, has become the need of the hour considering the rising heat and reducing green cover,” he said, also requesting villagers to assist him in protecting the saplings that he plants, and many oblige.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.title: Packers’ Jordan Love Reacts to Christian Watson’s Surprising Return From Broken Rib Injury
articles.summary: A hard hit late in the second quarter left Lambeau Field silent. On Thursday, against Carolina Panthers, Green Bay Packers‘ Christian Watson caught a 53-yard...
articles.body:
A hard hit late in the second quarter left Lambeau Field silent. On Thursday, against Carolina Panthers , Green Bay Packers ' Christian Watson caught a 53-yard pass and took a heavy hit from two defenders. He could not breathe and coughed up blood on the sideline.

Watson eventually had to be taken to the hospital but what happened next his teammate the Jordan Love.

Jorden Love shocked at Christian Watson's resurrection

Late in the second quarter, Christian Watson caught a 53-yard pass to reach 100 receiving yards. Two defenders hit him hard, knocking the wind out of him and causing him to cough up blood on the sideline. An ambulance took him to a hospital for a CT scan, which showed a broken rib but no internal bleeding.

Watson returned to Lambeau Field before the end of the third quarter to loud cheers. He caught two more passes, finishing with a career-high eight catches for 113 yards in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers. He later joked that his entrance felt like a WWE return where people greeted him like he had been resurrected.

Quarterback Jordan Love said he was shocked when Watson came back. "Man, that was crazy. It was a lot of people cheering… I didn't know what was happening. Then I see Christian running out, and he's just resurrected. It was great to see him," Love said .

Watson joked post-game about the dramatic return. "I was getting dap-ups like I was getting resurrected or something," Watson told reporters after the game .

Watson finished as the game's top receiver, setting a career high with 8 receptions for 113 yards on 10 targets. His tough fourth-quarter performance helped the Packers seal a 27-19 victory over Carolina.

Like Jordy Nelson, Watson is now Jordan Love's top deep target. He became the first Packers receiver since Nelson in 2014 to catch multiple 40-plus-yard touchdown passes in a single game.

Standing 6-foot-4 with sub-4.4 speed, Watson mirrors Nelson's lethal combination of height, speed, and boundary control, forcing opposing secondaries to play deep coverage.

Paired alongside Matthew Golden, Watson's production has created Green Bay's most potent dual-receiver setup since the 2014 Jordy Nelson–Randall Cobb pairing.

articles.title: Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display
articles.summary: Saturday's third round of the Mexico Open sees the USA's Andrew Novak build six-shot lead at PGA Tour event; France's Matthieu Pavon currently sits second in standings; watch live coverage of the final round of the Mexico Open from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Sunday
articles.body:
About the only thing Novak did wrong at Vidanta Vallarta was losing the handle on a club twirl at the par-five 12th while admiring a 279-yard shot that settled 20 feet away for an eagle.

That was part of his sublime stretch of three birdies and an eagle that extended his lead to seven shots. It was such a great day for Novak that even when he had a lie in the rough with a golf ball well below his feet, he hammered that out to six feet on the 14th for a birdie.

Novak ended the day on a 23-under 190, primed for his first individual title on the PGA Tour. His only other victory was teaming with Ben Griffin in the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year.

He had the low round of the day while playing in the last group, and goes into the final round coming off scores of 61-62.

"Very much the same, maybe a little sloppy at the end," Novak said of the two rounds. "But the putter saved it."

He holed a six-foot par on the 16th and made a 10-foot par putt on the 17th after coming up short.

Matthieu Pavon of France birdied his last two holes for a 65 to get within six shots. Doug Ghim had a 64 and was another shot behind.

Everyone is chasing Novak, who has made only three bogeys through 54 holes.
