articles.title: Lucknow@2040: Aiming for future perfect
articles.summary: Lucknow@2040: UPSCR six-district plan, metro and new corridors aim to boost connectivity and growth, while preserving Awadh’s heritage, culture and hospitality.
articles.body: By 2040, Lucknow could be one of the most distinctive metropolitan cities of North India – larger, faster and more connected, but still recognisably Lucknow with its heritage and culture intact.The challenge would not simply be to construct more roads, offices and housing, but also to decide what kind of city it should be.Lucknow has always carried contradictions comfortably. It is a city of expanding neighbourhoods and old mohallas, of govt institutions and private enterprises, of modern malls and centuries-old markets.Its reputation rests not only on monuments like Bada Imambara, but also on food, language, hospitality, craftsmanship and an unhurried social culture.The question for the next 14 years is simple: what should Lucknow become without ceasing to be Lucknow?NOT JUST A CAPITAL CITY, BUT A CAPITAL REGIONThe approval of the base map for the Uttar Pradesh State Capital Region (UPSCR) could mark the beginning of a bigger transformation — one in which Lucknow’s growth is no longer confined to the city but extends across a connected six-district economic region.UPSCR brings together Lucknow, Sitapur, Unnao, Hardoi, Barabanki and Rae Bareli, covering 26,741 sq km. The next step is approval of the regional plan, which will determine how transport, industry, housing, infrastructure and economic activity are coordinated across the region.If proper planning is followed over the next 15 years, UPSCR could look very different by 2040.Anupam Mittal, an architect, says, “Lucknow’s infrastructure is evolving from a centrally concentrated city to a more connected, multi-centred urban region. Radial roads, ring roads, Kisan Path, proposed Outer Ring Road, Green Corridor, and the State Capital Region are strengthening regional connectivity and enabling more controlled development.”Emerging townships such as Varun Vihar are expected to create new commercial and residential centres, reducing pressure on the existing central business district (CBD).Metro expansion and transit-oriented development will further improve connectivity and support higher-density development along transit routes.Together, these initiatives could transform Lucknow into a city with multiple, self-sustaining centres, reducing travel across the city and improving overall urban efficiency.ON THE FAST LANEBy 2040, the real measure of success could be how quickly a person or product moves across the region.Better highways, public transport, rail links, logistics infrastructure and planned urban corridors could gradually shrink economic distances between Lucknow and its neighbouring districts.A worker living in one district could access a job in another. A farmer could reach a processing centre faster. A manufacturer could move goods to a major market or airport more efficiently. A company setting up outside Lucknow could still access the capital’s talent, institutions and services.FLAGBEARER OF USD 1 TRILLION ECONOMY TARGETArvind Mohan, economist & dean, faculty of arts, Lucknow University, says that if Uttar Pradesh’s economy reaches the $1 trillion economy target or exceeds, Lucknow would majorly contribute to it.“If the $1 trillion economy target is achieved, some critical changes will happen, particularly in infrastructure. For example, one challenge for Uttar Pradesh is that its logistics infrastructure is not as developed as it should be,” he said.“Indeed, many of the expressways pass through Lucknow. All districts of Uttar Pradesh are connected by four-lane roads, and all district headquarters are connected to Lucknow. As logistics infrastructure is developed along these routes, Lucknow will certainly be a major beneficiary,” he added.“Lucknow has to play an important role in several ways. In major states, we have seen transformations. For example, Chandrababu Naidu transformed Andhra Pradesh at one stage. What he did was that, rather than marketing Andhra Pradesh as a whole, Hyderabad was marketed, and Hyderabad transformed itself in many ways. In particular, the IT sector and many other industries relocated to Hyderabad. Lucknow has a similar advantage,” he observed.“I’m sure that, at some stage, just like Hyderabad, Lucknow will have to be marketed. Lucknow has all the potential to become a city like Hyderabad at some point in time,” he said.“If you want to make Lucknow an IT city, one should understand that in the early 1990s, after Bangalore, when people were speculating about which city could become the next major destination for IT or IT-enabled services, Lucknow was considered a frontrunner for a number of reasons. It had all kinds of infrastructure and good schools. Everything needed in terms of manpower was there,” Arvind Mohan pointed out.“If you are looking at transforming Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow must play a major role. One area is logistics. Another major area of potential is IT, and yet another is the biotechnology revolution,” he said.“Lucknow has 12 national laboratories. I don’t think there is any other city that has that many national laboratories, along with so many industries in the surrounding area. There is huge potential for a biotechnology revolution, which is perhaps the next revolution after IT. So, Lucknow could become India’s first biotechnology city,” he added.He said that be it pharmaceuticals, IT or IT-enabled services, or biotechnology in general, these sectors need to be ignited in Lucknow, along with substantial improvements in infrastructure connectivity and logistics.EXPERT VIEWWhen Lucknow was established as the capital of Awadh, it was essentially an urban centre. The buildings, Hazratganj, institutional buildings, riverfront, and even residential buildings have historically been integral to the city’s urbanity.“It would be a grave mistake to treat historic buildings merely as heritage and keep them separated from the imagination of the emerging future of the city. The historical is the cultural identity and a fundamental anchor if we are to prepare ourselves to integrate cultural identity into futuristic development,” says Sonal Mithal, a conservation architect who has been working on architectural history and conservation of Lucknow buildings.“This will help project a vision for Lucknow whose future would be unique as it emerges from its culture. The need is to propose future urban projects that uphold the town planning initiatives taken in the first half of the 20th century and align with Awadhi culture,” says Mithal, who is a professor and chair of the master’s in Conservation and Regeneration programme at Ahmedabad’s CEPT University.“This can only happen if systematic and targeted studies are undertaken with a specific focus on historicity that has the potential to guide and propel the futures. Today’s citizens identify Lucknow through its food (designated as Unesco Creative City of Gastronomy on Oct 31, 2025), colonial and Nawabi history, the unique gharial ecosystem, riverine landscapes, post-independence history, and now its growing commerce and tourism, boom in real estate, technology, and infrastructure projects,” she says.“The time has come to bring these together, combining nature-cultures with technologies and economies,” says Mithal.With her students and colleagues, she has worked extensively on the architectural history and putting up forward-looking conservation proposals for Chhatar Manzil, Kaiserbagh, and the Residency, among others.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Springs Valley's Calvin Seitz goes back-to-back to win state cross country meet
articles.summary: Oregon-bound Calvin Seitz, most accomplished Springs Valley athlete since Larry Bird, wins second consecutive cross country state title, sets record.
articles.body:
TERRE HAUTE – Calvin Seitz won a cross-country state title a year ago by two-hundredths of a second. He left no doubt Saturday.

Seitz became Southern Indiana's first two-time champion, smashing a 46-year-old state meet record on the LaVern Gibson Championship Course. Seitz covered 5,000 meters in 14 minutes, 34.7 seconds and won by 25.7 seconds – third-biggest margin of victory since 1968.

After a 4:17 first mile, the only thing on the course near him was the GATER ... and driver of that lead vehicle had the pedal down.

See Calvin Seitz, Fort Wayne Carroll; Indiana high school boys cross country state champions

"I kind of knew it wasn't smart for me to go out and hang with him," said runner-up Jack Wilbourne, a junior at Signature, an Evansville charter school.

Seitz is the most decorated athlete out of Springs Valley High School since Larry Bird. The runner is headed to Oregon, where Cole Hocker stopped off in college en route to an Olympic gold medal.

Seitz is the first to win back-to-back since Carmel's Ben Veatch in 2014-15. Other multiple winners include North Central's Futsum Zienasellassie (2009-10-11), Franklin Central's Aaron Fisher (1998-99-2000) and Hammond's Rudy Chapa (1974-75).

"It's an honor to be among some of the greats," Seitz said. "There's just so many to pick from."

He said most meaningful was to share the moment with his family, including father Adam Seitz, a 10.4 ppg basketball scorer from 1998-2002 at the University of Evansville.

Seitz's time bettered the long-standing 14:42.3 by Owen Valley's Curt Carey at South Grove Golf Course, Indianapolis. Best at state on this course was 14:46.9 by Fishers' Sam Quagliaroli in 2024.

In the Nike XC Town Twilight race Oct. 3, Seitz (14:42.1) and Evansville Reitz's Carter Zieren (14:42.4) became the two fastest Hoosiers ever at LaVern Gibson.

Seitz climbed to No. 5 on the course's all-time list, behind four boys from the 2022 Nike Midwest Regional. Early on, he was challenging the record of 14:21.8 by Hunter Jones of Benzie Central (Mich.).

"It wasn't the plan," Seitz said. "But if that's how it worked out, that's how it worked out, you know?"

He was coming off a 14:30.70 regional time at Crawford County, where he broke the course record by 50 seconds and beat runner-up Zieren by 44 seconds.

Wilbourne's time was 15:00.4, followed by the Fort Wayne Carroll duo of Sam Sweet and Kai Feasel.

Carmel's Lucas Bartlett was fifth in 15:06.9 and Zieren sixth in 15:09.5. Jonah Kaul, also of Carmel, was eighth.

Fort Wayne Carroll, ranked 20 th nationally by DyeStat, placed three boys in the top seven and won the team title with 66 points. Carmel was second with 105, a score good enough to win in many years.

Defending champion Columbus North was third with 124 and Brownsburg fourth with 206.

"There's no defense, right? I would have set something up if I could," Carmel coach Colin Altevogt said of Carroll. "They're a really good team. We just wanted to come out and do what we could do."

In the past 15 state meets, the Greyhounds have finished first or second 12 times. They coped with some illnesses this season, Altevogt said.

"This has been one of our better teams, but this was a really strong year," he said. "We really ran well in October. On the last day of October, I feel we had our best race of the season."

Carmel will return to Terre Haute on Nov. 15 for the Midwest Regional in a bid to qualify for Nike nationals, set for Dec. 5 at Portland, Ore.

articles.title: Golden State Warriors Announce Injury Report vs. LA Clippers (Nov. 1)
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors began their six-game homestand on Friday with a huge comeback win over the Los Angeles Lakers.Steph Curry had a huge night, scoring...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors began their six-game homestand on Friday with a huge comeback win over the Los Angeles Lakers.

Steph Curry had a huge night, scoring 31 points to lead the Warriors to their third straight win. Their bench also came up big in erasing the Lakers' 25-point lead, combining for 50 points.

The Warriors are back in action on Sunday, welcoming the LA Clippers to the Chase Center.

Golden State Warriors Injury Report vs. Clippers

GettySteph Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors reacts after making a basket against the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California.

On Saturday, the Golden State Warriors released their injury report against the LA Clippers.

The Warriors have six players on their injury report, including major players like Steph Curry and Draymond Green .

Sunday's matchup is the first game of a back-to-back, so the Warriors ruled out Curry and Green to give them extra rest ahead of Monday's game against the Phoenix Suns .

Curry is dealing with a right knee injury, while Green is nursing a back issue.

The other four players on the injury report are Kristaps Porzingis , Jimmy Butler , Moses Moody and Gui Santos .

Porzingis continues to be away from the Warriors, and it's possible he won't ever suit up for the franchise again.

Butler and Moody are recovering from knee surgeries, though both are expected to return later this season.

Santos is listed as probable with left knee tendinitis. He was cleared for Friday's game, so it won't be surprising if he gets upgraded to available against the Clippers.

After a ho-hum summer, the Golden State Warriors entered the 2026-27 NBA season without a ton of expectations.

Steph Curry signed a two-year extension, but the Warriors roster wasn't built to contend for a playoff spot.

The Warriors began the season on the road against the Los Angeles Lakers. They were blown out at Crypto.com Arena, followed by two more losses to the Memphis Grizzlies and Phoenix Suns.

However, rookie Yaxel Lendebor g's inspired play and Curry's greatness helped Golden State beat the Denver Nuggets for their first win of the season.

They then beat the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this week before getting their revenge on the Lakers on Friday.

articles.title: LPGA Maybank Championship: Miyu Yamashita holds off Yan Liu to defend her title at the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club
articles.summary: Japan's Miyu Yamashita holds off China's long-hitting Yan Liu to become the first back-to-back champion in Maybank Championship history at Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC)
articles.body:
The 2025 Women's Open winner and third-round leader ended with a 72-hole total of 22-under after a final-round 68 on the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course.

The Japanese golfer sank five birdies with just the one bogey at the par-4 ninth in a near-perfect week where she led from Friday's second round until the final hole.

It was the 25-year-old's fifth career title and second in the LPGA Tour this season after she took a wire-to-wire, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open at Royal Mayfair in Edmonton, Alberta in August.

"Today was an especially tough round for me," Yamashita said.

"Yan Liu hits the ball with so much power and distance. She was making birdies early and hitting aggressive shots. I felt like I couldn't let my guard down for a single moment until the final putt dropped on the 18th."

On the back of Saturday's 63 to surge into contention, Yan kept in touch throughout the final round as she also shot a 68, but couldn't quite close the gap to the nerveless Yamashita and finished at 18-under.

Pauline Roussin-Bouchard, who led after the first round, shot 69 Sunday and was tied for third with amateur player Marisa Tojai (67) of Thailand a further shot back.

Australia's Robyn Choi was fifth at 17-under after a 69.

Yamashita's win was her third LPGA Tour title of the season, following victories at the Meijer LPGA Classic and CPKC Women's Open.

articles.title: Green Party at a "crossroads", says former co-leader Adrian Ramsay
articles.summary: Adrian Ramsay suggested the party needs to focus on its "core values", including environmental issues.
articles.body:
The Green Party is at a "crossroads" and needs to focus on its "core values", a former party co-leader has told the BBC, weeks after members adopted a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism.

Adrian Ramsay suggested the Greens need their policies to appeal to a majority of British voters if they want to bring the "environmental changes that we need" and advised against taking an approach that risks being "quite divisive".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski responded by saying there was "no environmental justice without social, racial and economic justice".

The motion, which Polanski did not take part in or vote upon, defined Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" that had led to the "disenfranchisement and destruction" of Palestinians.

I would not have voted for Zionism motion, Polanski says

It backed the creation of a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.

Members of the Green Party of England and Wales adopted the policy motion last month.

It led to a backlash from some Jewish groups, as well as criticism from senior Green figures, including Ramsay and other Green MPs.

Israel's foreign ministry said it had banned Polanski , who is Jewish, from entering the country.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission also wrote to the Green Party asking for more information about the motion after concerns were raised by dozens of Labour and Lib Dem MPs and Jewish campaigners.

Labour later said it would end power-sharing agreements with the Greens on local councils, unless its councillors disowned the policy.

Speaking to Newscast , Ramsay replied "no, it's not" when asked if he thought Zionism is racist before adding he agreed with Polanski and others in believing that what is happening in Gaza is "appalling".

The MP for Waveney Valley, who joined the party in 1998, said he does think Israel has a right to exist, something Polanski has stopped short of saying.

Ramsay also said he has made it clear he is "deeply uncomfortable" with the motion adopted and suggested there is an "opportunity to take some action in relation to the motion in the run-up" to the party's spring conference next year.

He said the question now is how Polanski and the party as a whole responds to the motion.

Ramsay said: "I think there's a real crossroads point for the party at the moment.

"One option is to sort of dig in more down this approach, not only in relation to this motion, but I think that there's a risk it brings with it - a quite divisive, a quite internally focused approach to politics."

Ramsay said this is "perhaps seen from small groups of people on the hard left of politics who go around different parties try to influence how those parties are run".

He added: "What I want to see is the party really focus back in on our core aims as a party and our core values."

Ramsay said this includes ensuring the party is "consensus-building in how we approach our politics" and that "we engage the grassroots of our membership".

He added the party needs to be "very externally focused, because we're only going to be able to bring the environmental changes that we need to have to safeguard our society for now and for the future if the majority of the British public come behind that".

Ramsay served as co-leader of the Greens from 2021 to 2025 alongside Carla Denyer, who is also now an MP.

He unsuccessfully stood on a joint ticket with fellow MP Ellie Chowns in 2025, with the pair losing to Polanski in the leadership contest .

Polanski, who missed the conference vote to unsuccessfully campaign for election in a Westminster by-election, previously said he wants to see the "imperfect" motion amended in future.

However, he said the "substantial part of the motion", that "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by a racist ideology" was "obvious". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

articles.title: Paige Spiranac unloads her Halloween content on America, Jenn Sterger as Wednesday Addams & Capturing Bigfoot
articles.summary: Paige Spiranac's Halloween content dominates as unranked USC stuns Ohio State football and the Capturing Bigfoot documentary reveals surprises.
articles.body: I'm back from vacation and in need of a vacation from the vacation. I spent a good part of the day yesterday in the car and missed a lot of college football action trying to make it back in time for our little guy to go trick or treating. That was a success and, after I unpacked, I was able to catch the unranked Tar Heels and a single and focused Bill Belichick nearly upset No. 1 Miami. Bill and company almost pulled it off. Everyone knows it only really counts if you pull it off. Which brings me to another of the games I caught the end of, unranked USC defeating No. 2-ranked Ohio State. Obviously, the Buckeyes were once again highly overrated. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! You hate to see Ohio State lose a game on the road that they should win. Sadly, you're going to hear all kinds of excuses about Julian Sayin being injured. Bottom line, they couldn't get the job done. The beard dye is fading in Columbus. Paige Spiranac unloads her Halloween content on America Now to more important matters than the sad state of Ohio State football. Paige Spiranac putting her love of Halloween on display for all of America. If you're going to do such a thing, you have to go all out. It's safe to say that the top golf influencer on the planet, and some are even saying the best influencer to have ever done it, went all out. PAIGE SPIRANAC GIVES PEOPLE WHAT THEY DIDN'T KNOW THEY NEEDED: HER YOGURT BOWL RECIPE Are we still declaring winners of Halloween and other holidays? I don't know. I'm never on top of those sorts of things. Although I do strongly believe in recognizing greatness. Paige's effort here is unmatched. The numbers speak for themselves. She showed up and kept the pressure on everyone else trying to compete. If that's not how you win Halloween, I don't know the rules anymore. Capturing Bigfoot I watched the "Capturing Bigfoot" documentary when it came out on Bigfoot Day, which is October 20, for those who didn't know. The documentary is about the famous 1967 Patterson-Gimlin Bigfoot footage. The footage that supposedly shows Bigfoot out for a stroll in California. There were a few things about the Patterson-Gimlin film that I didn’t know before I sat down and watched it. On the top of that list is that people still believed, at least before this documentary, that footage was real. That blew me away. I thought it was agreed upon long ago that it was fake. Apparently not. There were some out there who believed it was real video evidence of Bigfoot. The documentary (spoiler alert) shows another piece of footage that was believed to be a test run a year before Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin filmed the footage we have all seen. I debated whether I would write a standalone article about the documentary and I decided that it belonged in "America's Best Daily Column." I said in a prior edition of Sunday Screencaps that I would watch it after all, and I did purchase it and waste my time watching it. CARMEN ELECTRA OFFICIALLY KICKS OFF HALLOWEEN SEASON AT A GAS STATION, POSTGAME POLICE CHASE & BALL-SAC Back to the doc. Another piece of information I learned about the Patterson-Gimlin film was how much money it generated when it first came out. I had no idea that it was shown in venues around the country. I didn’t get into Bigfoot because of the Patterson-Gimlin film. As I've mentioned before, it was the fine work and incredible confidence in the existence of Bigfoot (despite an overwhelming lack of evidence) by the folks on the show "Finding Bigfoot" that got me hooked. So, if you're interested in learning more about the Patterson-Gimlin film, the documentary will fill you in. They spoke to many people involved in and around the famous footage. If you're hoping this documentary finally debunks the Patterson-Gimlin film, I'd point you at the original footage. That does a decent job of debunking it all by itself. Oh, and one more thing I learned from this doc. The Bigfoot in the Patterson-Gimlin is female and has boobs. I got your meat - Scott in Ridgeland SC writes: SeanJo – hope you had a great weekend off. Been away from home quite a bit so first grill chance I’ve had in a while and all is good, beautiful sunset, flood tide coming in (no redfish running unfortunately), bottle of pinot noir ready to go and hoping the Gamecocks come back and win (they did)! Maybe a little dark liquor later and yes that ribeye was way bigger than I thought it was going to be. All is right with the world. SeanJo Nice meat, Scott. We had a great week off. I'm glad you got a chance to fire up the grill and that it happened during a win. Keep sending in your meat. ------------------------- That is all I have on this first day of November. Yesterday was the Super Bowl for Instagram models, and they took Paige Spiranac's lead by dumping out their best Halloween content. My Panthers have already lost this week. You know what's nice about losing on Thursday night? You can focus on your fantasy football team losing on Sunday. That said, the Panthers are still on top of the NFC South and have the rest of the division right where they want them. There's a lot of football left to be played and, at 3-4, they're still in it. Yes, I am ignoring the in-season coaching changes and what that says about the current state of the franchise. I'm choosing to remain positive. Again, there's a lot of football left. articles.title: Mexico Open: Andrew Novak cruises to title for maiden individual PGA Tour triumph at Vidanta Vallarta
articles.summary: Sunday's final round of PGA Tour's Mexico Open sees USA's Andrew Novak claim title victory, his first individual triumph on PGA Tour; Novak, whose only previous tour victory came at last year's Zurich Classic pairs event alongside Ben Griffin, finished on a tournament record 25-under-par
articles.body:
Novak staked himself to a big lead with rounds of 61-62 the previous two days, and it was going to take something special to track him down. But with a soft bogey on the 10th hole, his lead was down to three over Steven Fisk and Mexico-born Norwegian Kristoffer Ventura.

And then it was effectively over. Novak hit a greenside bunker shot to four feet on the par-5 12th at Vidanta Vallarta, drove the 13th green to 15 feet for a two-putt birdie, and he ended his decisive run with a 45-foot birdie putt on the 14th.

"That kind of really settled everything," Novak said. "Just happy with how I played today. I thought I grinded it out pretty well."

Fisk and Ventura each closed with a 63, and it was particularly meaningful for Ventura. He was at No. 108 in the FedEx Cup Fall, knowing only the top 100 keep full cards for 2027. The runner-up finish, his best as an individual, moved him to No. 76 and locked up his card.

Mackenzie Hughes of Canada shot 66 and wound up in a tie for fourth when Doug Ghim, playing in the final group, made double bogey on the 18th hole. Hughes moved up to No. 101, a manageable spot with three tournaments remaining.

"Gives me a bit of momentum for the last three," Hughes said. "Obviously, I still know I need more points and I need to keep climbing, but today was a big step in the right direction."

Hughes tied for fourth with Ben Griffin, who was Novak's partner when they won the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year. Griffin (67) was waiting on the 18th green when Novak finished.

"I loved Zurich and everything about that tournament. That's so fun," Novak said. "But it is nice to have one by myself, too. This is one I've been working for for a while. Obviously not a great season for how I wanted it to go, but this is a nice way to kind of finish."

The outcome was never really in doubt, though Novak must have wondered if anything was going to go his way. On the third hole, the easiest of the par 5s, Novak's second shot plugged into the lip and he could only nudge back into the bunker, leading to par. He missed two other birdie chances from just inside 10 feet on the front nine.

"I played really well on the front and didn't get much out of it," he said.

Novak waited his turn, and three straight birdies was more than enough to send him on his way. He moved from No 89 to No 53 in the FedEx Cup, making him practically a lock to at least be in a pair of $20m (£14m) signature events next year at Pebble Beach and Riviera.

The victory also assures Novak will start the 2028 on the upper Championship Series.

Kihei Akina, the 20-year-old sophomore at Brigham Young University (BYU), closed with a 59 and finished 15th. It was his third top-20 finish on the PGA Tour this year.

articles.title: Three-star wide receiver decommits from FSU Seminoles
articles.summary: Three-star wide receiver Majay Thompson has decommitted from the FSU Seminoles. He committed back in June.
articles.body:
The FSU Seminoles have suffered another blow to their 2027 recruiting class, with three-star wide receiver Majay Thompson decommitting on Sunday, announcing the news on social media. The news comes after they lost to the Clemson Tigers on Saturday.

"After conversations with my people, i've decided to decommit and reopen my recruitment," he wrote. "I appreciate everyone who has supported me throughout this journey. Excited for what's next!"

Thompson committed to FSU on June 19, picking the Seminoles over the Georgia Bulldogs , Alabama Crimson Tide , and Wake Forest Demon Deacons. He also recently visited the Virginia Tech Hokies.

He is ranked as the No. 530 overall player and No. 71 wide receiver in the 247Sports composite. The Shelby native is also the No. 19 player from North Carolina.

His departure leaves FSU with 14 commitments in the 2027 recruiting cycle, with four-star Sean Green as their only wide receiver commit. Thompson is the eighth decommit for FSU this cycle.

247Sports now ranks FSU's 2027 recruiting class as the 50th best in the country and the 15th best in the ACC. Seven of their 14 commits are four-star prospects.

articles.title: HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final: Julien Sale secures title, Hamish Brown crowned Road to Mallorca No 1 and DP World Tour cards confirmed
articles.summary: HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final sees France's Julien Sale claim title and Denmark's Hamish Brown finish top of the Road to Mallorca Rankings; Sale ends year second in rankings and will now step up to golf's DP World Tour for the first time in his career
articles.body:
Frenchman Sale, who was guaranteed promotion to the DP World Tour before the season finale in Mallorca, posted his second 65 of the week to reach 22 under par, four strokes clear of the Brown, who narrowly held onto solo second to capture the season-long title.

Sale ends the year second in the rankings and will now step up to golf's DP World Tour for the first time in his career.

He becomes the fifth player from France to win the Grand Final after Clément Sordet (2017), Benjamin Hebert (2014), Mike Lorenzo-Vera (2007) and Nicolas Joakimides (1997).

The 29-year-old started the day with a one-stroke advantage and fired four front-nine birdies to take control at Club de Golf Alcanada.

A gain on the par-five 12th further extended his advantage before he dropped his only shot of the day on the next.

He responded well, however, with three birdies in his final six holes helping him to his second HotelPlanner Tour triumph of 2026, after his win on home soil at the Le Vaudreuil Golf Challenge earlier this year.

He said: "Coming this week, I didn't have much stress because I knew I was inside the top 15 and the goal was to win the tournament and obviously try to finish number one on the ranking.

"I was going to have fun already tonight but now I'm going to enjoy it even more with my family here."

Brown becomes the fifth Dane to win the Road to Mallorca after Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen (2024), Marcus Helligkilde (2021), Joachim B Hansen (2018) and Thomas Bjørn (1995).

The 27-year-old posted a closing five-under 67 in Alcúdia to reach 18 under par for the week and held onto solo second after South African MJ Daffue saw his birdie putt slide by on the 72nd hole.

"It means a lot," said Brown. It's been a proper grind again. Ultimately, I couldn't win today thanks to a good Frenchman who played extremely well.

"It's just a day where you can't really control your thoughts. All you're thinking about is what they need to do or what's going to happen.

"It gives me a lot of confidence. I had a tough year last year on the DP World Tour, but I wasn't too far away, I thought.

"It's just moments throughout a season that need to go your way and I'm not scared of it for next year. I'm quite looking forward to it because I know what it what it is now. I know what I need to do and not to do.

"I'm trying to just expect more of myself."

Top 15 on Road to Mallorca earn DP World Tour cards

Dutchman Lars van der Vight, a two-time HotelPlanner Tour winner this season, ends the year as No 3, with another two-time victor, Sweden's Christofer Blomstrand , in fourth.

MJ Daffue , who won twice at the start of the year in South Africa and India, rounds out the top five with Spaniard Pablo Ereño in sixth.

Tapio Pulkkanen (seventh) returns to the DP World Tour at the first time of asking and is joined by Adam Wallin (eighth), Liam Nolan (ninth) and John Gough (10th).

Sebastian Friedrichsen ends the year in 11th position after sealing his breakthrough win in Portugal and is joined by Englishman Will Enefer in 12th.

Marc Warren delivered during the back nine on Sunday with a tied-for-fifth finish helping him climb seven places to 13th.

Andrew Wilson ends the year in 14th while Frenchman Maxence Giboudot held onto the all-important 15th position to confirm his spot on the DP World Tour for the first time.

articles.title: Jon Rahm questions and great golf values: Tour Confidential
articles.summary: In this Tour Confidential, GOLF's writers discuss what question they would ask of Jon Rahm, where you can find a great golf value, and more.
articles.body:
Check in every week for the unfiltered opinions of our writers and editors as they break down the hottest topics in the sport, and join the conversation by tweeting us at @golf_com . This week, we discuss Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia, WTGL and more.

1. This week's Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, the first event of the DP World Tour playoffs, is headlined by Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton, and Rahm and Hatton are just a couple of the former LIV players about to make their first start since announcing they won't be a part of LIV 2.0. You get one question to ask those guys in their pre-tournament press conference: What is it?

Josh Schrock, associate news editor ( @Schrock_And_Awe ): I would ask Rahm what I asked him at the PGA Championship this year: "What did you learn from your decision to go to LIV?" In May, he took a beat and said that was "for him to know." Would still love the answer now that his LIV time is over.

James Colgan, news and features editor ( @jamescolgan26 ): I'd love to ask the following Q: Why did you leave? I think we all know the real answer is "money" — but these players' careers will be defined by their decisions with LIV, and I think their accounting of why is important for future generations of golfers to know.

Josh Sens, senior writer ( @JoshSens ): Aside from any flack you caught from fans and commentators, what was the worst thing about moving to LIV?

Nick Piastowski, senior editor ( @nickpia ): All good answers about questions! Let's try a different route, in case we get some no comments there. How about: How would you now explain LIV Golf to someone who's been living under a rock since, say, 2026?

2. Rahm left for LIV as the defending Masters champion but has failed to win a major since. Fair or not, LIV's level of competition — and whether it kept players sharp enough for majors — became a frequent topic of debate. How do you expect Rahm to play now? Will no longer being tied to LIV make any difference?

Schrock: It's hard to say. It depends how he preps. What does his DP World Tour schedule look like before the four majors in 2027? I don't think it's unfair to say that being on LIV played some role in his major play. He's also still one of the top players in the world and will be a factor in majors moreso than he has been.

Colgan: I think he's a great player who has a lot of great golf ahead of him. I do think he'll play better. I do think being in a more meritocratic environment will make a difference.

Sens: Like James, I expect he'll play better, but less for physical reasons than mental ones. Once the distractions of all the LIV-related questions fade into the background and he falls back into a rhythm, I suspect his head will be in a better place. If I were his sports psychologist, I'd recommend this as a first step: admit to yourself — and possibly even to the public — that you did it for the money and the money only, and that you realize now that that was a mistake. That playing for the love of competition is what propelled you to greatness in the first place. I'd think that kind of honesty would be freeing. Not that I'm holding my breath waiting for it.

Piastowski: Man, Sens' answer here is pretty great. Maybe playing LIV events had something to do with Rahm's major record. Maybe it didn't. Who's to say he'd be 0-fer if he'd been playing PGA Tour golf? But coming to every major and being asked about LIV in some shape or form — or being reminded about it by the fans — had to weigh on him. Just for that reason, I expect him to play better.

3. The WTGL — Women's Team Golf League — kicks off its first matchup of its inaugural season at the SoFi Center on Sunday with Michelle Wie West's LA team taking on Lydia Ko's New York squad. Do you see the WTGL having similar success as the TGL, which begins its third season later this year? What's the key for the women's league to thrive?

Schrock: I hope it does. It's a great platform to showcase some personalities on the tour and for people to get to know the players outside of the majors. But not having Nelly and not having the women play on the same team as the men I think will be a big miss. I hope they can overcome it in Year 1 and perhaps integrate next winter (with Nelly in the fold!)

Colgan: I still haven't gotten a single compelling reason for why a co-ed TGL league is worse and less profitable than two separate gendered leagues.

Sens: Sadly, I think the past has proven that even when the women's game puts out as good or better a product than the men, the same level of fan interest just isn't there. So, no. I don't see the women's league having success similar to the men.

Piastowski: Why — WHY? — are they playing on NFL Sundays? In looking at the schedule, the WTGL goes up against either Sunday NFL or Monday NFL in half of its 10 matches. Every non-football league has trouble with interest in the fall, let alone a new one. I also agree with my colleagues above — let's play mixed TGL.

4. Readers can check out the rosters for each WTGL team here . Which squad are you most looking forward to watching, and why?

Schrock: It's L.A. just for Wie West. It was awesome to see her tee it up twice this year before saying goodbye, even if she didn't perform how she wanted. She's one of golf's great stars of the past century, and it's cool she'll still be in our lives even if it's only in simulator format.

Colgan: Motor City! Jeeno Thitikul is an amazing character who deserves the full shine of the golf world. This league will be great for her.

Sens: Good choices above. Next, I'd go with the Atlanta Drive. These events depend heavily on the quality of the banter. Most professional golfers aren't particularly good at banter. But Charley Hull is.

Piastowski: Easy. Boston Common, featuring Megan Khang, who said this at a pre-WTGL press conference: "I will admit I probably will drop a couple explicit words. … Thankfully, there's a little delay. There's a little [bleep] button, and that will be my best friend."

5. Sergio Garcia announced he will join the DP World Tour and is open to a return to the PGA Tour. His lengthy statement posted to social media was met by some criticism — including from pro Eddie Pepperell — due to the infamous ways Garcia exited the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. What are your thoughts on Sergio's statement and return? And is the way in which some former LIV players are received a major storyline for next season, or an overblown one?

Schrock: It's definitely a major storyline. I think some guys will be received well, depending on how they left and how they opt to return to the ecosystem. We saw how Brooks was welcomed back by pretty much everyone with open arms. That's a product of who he is and how he left without trying to torch his former tours. Some, like Sergio, took a different path and things might be frostier on re-entry.

Colgan: It's overdone. The vast majority of these guys care far more about their own business than anybody else's. The bad (good?) news for Sergio is that his career is almost assuredly in its last gasp already, so there won't be too much crow to eat.

Sens: Statements on social media are easy. I don't put much stock in Garcia's. Let's see how things play out. My guess is that the reception players get will be largely in keeping with how these players were viewed before they left. Those that were well liked should be able to fall back easily into fans' favor. Those that weren't will have a tougher go. I think it's fair to say that Garcia didn't rank high among fan favorites. Whether his reception becomes a major story will hinge on how he responds when he starts getting the first Bronx cheers, and how he conducts himself if he plays poorly. His track record suggests he'll make some more news along those lines.

Piastowski: The fans will be interested in the return of Garcia and others. There will be stories about it. There will be curiosity. But I like Colgan's answer: The pros won't care — much. I do think, though, Garcia could have won over a few folks by not completely glossing over his exit and what tour he's been on since 2022.

6. Our Alan Bastable wrote about Stow Acres Country Club, a 27-hole public facility 30 miles west of Boston that recently offered a special of 50-cent greens fees for nine holes. While a better deal might be tough to find, what's your favorite value round you've played in 2026?

Schrock: I didn't play as much golf as I wanted in 2026, but I always liked going home to play the muni that I grew up on and worked at throughout high school: The Greens at Redmond in Redmond, Oregon. Check it out if you're in the Bend area!

Colgan: Amazing question. I snuck out for 18 holes walking at the Lake Placid Club, which has a few great holes allegedly designed by Alister MacKenzie, on a glorious May afternoon earlier this year. I played in 2.5 hours, and since the golf staff was out for the day by the time I arrived, I paid by leaving a $20 on the counter.

Sens: Waverley Golf Club on the North Island of New Zealand. Roughly $20 bucks for a wild and wonderful course that could easily command a couple hundred dollars in the U.S.

Piastowski: Gonna go a different route here, for obvious reasons. The best value round I watched came at the end of July, when I walked with the only country club housed inside a homeless shelter. You can watch the video of it all by scrolling immediately down .

articles.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg joins Wilt Chamberlain club after career night vs. Clippers
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is already finding his name next to some of the greatest players in franchise history after a monster night agai...
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is already finding his name next to some of the greatest players in franchise history after a monster night against the Los Angeles Clippers .

The first-year forward erupted for a career-high 37 points in Golden State's 124-112 win on Sunday night at Chase Center. Lendeborg was nearly unstoppable, shooting 13-of-19 from the field, 6-of-11 from three and 5-of-6 from the free-throw line while adding six assists, four rebounds and a steal in 34 minutes.

According to ESPN Insights , it was the most points by a Warriors rookie in a game since Stephen Curry dropped 42 in 2010.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The big night also pushed Lendeborg into rare company. He is now averaging 22.3 points per game, making him just the third player in franchise history to average at least 20 points over his first seven career games. The only others to do it are Hall of Famers Wilt Chamberlain , who averaged 37.4 points in 1959-60, and Rick Barry, who put up 22.9 in 1965-66.

Lendeborg's performance was even more impressive considering the circumstances . The Warriors played without both Curry and Draymond Green, leaving the rookie to shoulder much of the scoring load.

It was also a major bounce-back effort. Lendeborg struggled in Friday's win over the Los Angeles Lakers , finishing with six points and five turnovers before fouling out in 24 minutes.

"I had no impact on the game whatsoever (on Friday), and then the depth came in, and they took care of everything," Lendeborg told reporters .

He had plenty of help on Sunday, too. De'Anthony Melton added 21 points on six 3-pointers, while Brandin Podziemski and Brandon Williams each chipped in 17. Golden State shot 53.5% from the field and knocked down 22 threes.

Rui Hachimura led the Clippers with 24 points, and Kobe Sanders added 16.

The Warriors selected Lendeborg with the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft out of Michigan, where he averaged 15.1 points and 6.8 rebounds last season. Some viewed his age as a drawback, as he entered the league at 24, but the Summer League MVP has been a polished contributor from day one .

The win was Golden State's fourth straight, improving the Warriors to 4-3 after an 0-3 start. They will look to keep the momentum going when they host the Phoenix Suns on Monday.

articles.title: LIV Golf: Bryson DeChambeau hopeful league 'can exist forever' and says his Masters loss to Rory McIlroy helped him grow
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau is optimistic about LIV Golf's future, and revealed the league's proposed new iteration, LIV 2.0, is not intended to be a competitor to the PGA Tour; DeChambeau also believes his loss to Rory McIlroy at the 2025 Masters has helped him grow as a person
articles.body:
While the likes of Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton and Sergio Garcia are among those to have indicated they will not be participating in the league's new iteration , DeChambeau, who has been tight-lipped on the matter, spoke of his optimism about the future of the league.

LIV has undergone a restructuring since the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced it was ending its financing of the circuit at the end of the 2026 season.

The league later announced its intentions to relaunch in 2027 after it secured a package of £223.57m ($300m) from its new lead investors, BC Partners, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

Reflecting on his time with the tour, DeChambeau spoke in a wide-ranging interview on the Figuring Out with Raj Shamani podcast about the league's recent financial issues.

"The team golf stuff I was very excited about," DeChambeau said to Shamani. "I really cared and I still do care about the team golf stuff.

"The top co. [company] wasn't really managing that effectively. I know that now. I didn't know that during the time.

"Our teams were doing very well. Our teams generated almost $29m (£21.61m) last year in revenue.

"We had £15.65m ($21m) in costs from payment of players and expenses and travel and everything. So, we made £5.96m ($8m) EBIDTA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) last year.

"The teams were doing well. But all of the player payments and everything got pushed down to the teams when they went bankrupt, because the top co. [company] wasn't being run effectively.

"No fault to each other, but we thought there was a lot more capital that was going to be at play from the guys that were funding it."

Uncertainty still remains over what LIV 2.0 could look like; however, DeChambeau stressed the new circuit would not be a 'competitor' to the PGA Tour.

"The business model makes a lot of sense," he said. "We're actually working through that right now for this new model.

"It will make full financial sense. No funny business, no nothing.

"It's going to be done right, and this is going to be a league that exists hopefully forever."

He added: "It's not combative; we're not trying to compete against the [PGA] Tour, we want to be creative.

"We want to bring value to anywhere and everywhere in the golf market across the world."

DeChambeau: McIlroy Masters loss made me a better person

During the podcast, DeChambeau also spoke about how being humbled on the golf course has helped him grow as a person.

He and Rory McIlroy duked it out in the final round of the 2025 Masters. DeChambeau ultimately fell away while the Northern Irishman ended his long wait to win his first Green Jacket.

Prior to that, DeChambeau outlasted McIlroy by a shot at Pinehurst No 2 in 2024, to win his second US Open title.

"If there's one thing that people don't realise about me - I think this is something that's a good little point, too - it's not that I like being humbled, I like having the perspective, right?" DeChambeau said.

"It sucks getting humbled. Right? Everybody doesn't like it, but it needs to happen. In order for me to improve in life, I need to be humbled.

"There's no question. And you know, whether it's me losing the Masters to Rory [McIlroy] or him losing to me at the US Open when I won, it's so good for us.

"I think that's why golf is so great because it does humble us, no matter what. You can think you're the best in the world, and the next day you can't go ahead and hit a golf shot. I think that's what's so beautiful about it.

"That difficult moment is what honestly has helped shape me into a better person today. So, if I didn't have that, I wouldn't be the person I am today."

articles.title: Andrew Novak cruises in Mexico, the Blades Brown knighting rumor, and Fifa Laopakdee heads back to the Masters
articles.summary: Andrew Novak shot 61-62 across 36 holes to claim a five-shot victory at the Mexico Open, while a wild Blades Brown rumor stole the spotlight.
articles.body: This year's Mexico Open did not deliver the same incredible level of drama we witnessed at Vidanta Vallarta a year ago, thanks to Andrew Novak transforming into prime Tiger Woods, but you can't complain about a guy going on an absolute heater en route to his first individual title on the PGA Tour. Blades Brown was in the field in Mexico and finished a respectable T-19, and during the event, an unsubstantiated yet absolutely hysterical rumor about the teenage phenom made the rounds in the golf world. It involves actual swords, knighting, and meetings around a round table. In New Zealand, our eyes were fortunate enough to get a look at Te Arai Links for the Asia-Pacific Amateur. While the golf course was the main character, looking like a piece of land that could only be found on a planet not named Earth, Fifa Laopakdee went back-to-back, earning a Masters invite for the second consecutive year. Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com. Andrew Novak dominates south of the border Andrew Novak was in the midst of a lackluster 2026 season before arriving in Mexico. The Wofford College grad missed the cut in three of the four majors, didn't play the weekend at The Players, and managed just two Top 10s in 25 starts if you excluded the team event Zurich Classic. To say something clicked at the Mexico Open would be disrespectful to his performance. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE After an opening round 67 put him five shots back of the lead, he woke up on Friday and decided that over the next 36 holes he was going to turn into the best putter on the property and essentially not miss a thing. Novak led the field in strokes gained: putting in both rounds two and three, picking up over 5.6 shots on the greens alone on Friday, posting scores of 61-62. When you shoot 19-under across 36 holes as Novak did, you're going to separate from the field, which is exactly what happened before ultimately earning a five-shot victory. Steven Fisk and Kristoffer Ventura both shot final rounds of 63 only to lose by five. That has to be quite the feeling. Novak, who won the 2025 Zurich Classic alongside teammate Ben Griffin, moves up to 53rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings. Finishing inside the Top 50 is huge, with those players earning spots in full-field and signature events in 2027. Blades Brown is a big swords guy, allegedly When your first name is Blades, you're destined to play golf at some level. Blades Brown just so happens to ooze so much talent that he decided to skip out on college, turn professional as a teenager, and earn his PGA Tour card before turning 20. In order to get to the level Brown has climbed to in such fast fashion, one has to have a team around them, and young Mr. Blades allegedly takes the formation of said team very, very seriously. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK GOLF COVERAGE THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Andy Johnson of The Fried Egg has heard a rumor involving Brown and his team, and it may be the greatest thing my 33-year-old ears have ever heard. During an episode of The Shotgun Start podcast last week, Johnson emphasized that the rumor is unsubstantiated, but that doesn't make it any less incredible. "Everybody has their teams and everything in golf, your trainer, coaches, your agents, your parents, and I'm hearing that Blades has an interesting aspect to his team," Johnson began. "In order to become a part of the team, you have to get knighted, and you're given a sword. So everyone on his team, whether it's his swing coach, his personal trainer, his agent, they have swords, and they commence and discuss Blades Brown business around a round table. "Mike Sposa is his equipment guy for Callaway, and he was given a sword, and you become knighted to become part of Blades' team." Johnson went on to say that it is Brown's parents doing the alleged knighting, which makes it a little less awkward, yet still objectively hilarious. Blades handing out actual blades to his support staff is the type of golf content we live for. Fifa Laopakdee gets another go at Augusta National The Asia-Pacific Amateur may have moved from Dubai to New Zealand, but the winner remained the same. Thailand's Fifa Laopakdee defended his title at one of the most prestigious amateur events in the world at Te Arai, winning by three shots after a wildly impressive 63 to begin the tournament. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER With the victory, Laopakdee earned a spot in both the 2027 Masters and 2027 Open Championship at St. Andrews; not exactly the worst two events to add to the schedule for a college player at Arizona State. "I feel like I'm more proud of myself this year because I never stopped believing in myself, and even though I had a tough year," Laopakdee said after his victory. "I literally didn't win a single thing since March. I just keep telling myself that I've still got it. "Shout out to my friends, my family, my coaches, my teammates, that still believe in me and push me hard every day. This win means a lot because I'm able to prove to myself that I've still got it." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Laopakdee missed the cut at both the Masters and Open a year ago, and it will be interesting to see how another year and another impressive win under his belt suits him on the biggest of stages his second time around.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers News: Ty’Ron Hopper is having his moment
articles.summary: A third round pick in 2024, Hopper is finally paying dividends.
articles.body:
Ty'Ron Hopper was famously a virtually invisible man for his first two years in Green Bay.

You've heard the numbers, but permit me to recount them again. Over his first two seasons with the Packers, Hopper lined up for just 144 snaps on defense. He played more on special teams, but considering how many of his reps came on kickoff coverage and return, a good number of those snaps involved him doing literally nothing as the ball sailed into the end zone for a touchback. Prior to injuries to Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin, there were 21 games in Hopper's career where he was active but never appeared on defense. In 15 games, he recorded zero tackles — despite being in uniform and on the field, he had the same measurable impact on the game that you or I did.

But with those aforementioned injuries clearing the way, Hopper has blossomed. Thursday night he had a remarkable statistical performance, recording multiple passes defensed, an interception, and a sack, an outing only duplicated in recent Packers history by Charles Woodson, which is pretty excellent company to keep.

None of this, for what it's worth, is evidence that Hopper is about to become a core part of the Packers defense. Anybody can have a good game or two; putting together consistently good performances is what separates the metaphorical men from the boys. But this is far more than we've seen from Hopper to this point, and, if nothing else, it should be evidence that he can do good things for the defense when he's on the field.

Considering how little he's been on the field so far, that's a huge step forward.

Whatever patience the Packers had with Hopper is paying off.

Hopper had the game of his life, and he appears to be rounding into form at an opportune time.

They've got the cloud of dust part down pat, I'll give them that.

I have no idea what Brian Gutekunst is going to do at the trade deadline, but nothing about this season would surprise me anymore.

Week 8 was about as wild a week of NFL football as you're going to see. Almost nothing feels like an overreaction.

We're just past Halloween, but it looks like Thing from the Addams Family is still sticking around.

I don't know if John Williams is the future at center, but he's been remarkably solid in two games so far. Considering that he'd never played the spot in an actual game before, that's pretty amazing!
